2.15.57.s: athāsmā araṇī prayacchann āha vācaṃyamo bhaviṣyasi sam̐śādhi yat te sam̐śiṣyam iti
2.15.57.d: अथास्मा अरणी प्रयच्छन्न् आह वाचंयमो भविष्यसि सँशाधि यत् ते सँशिष्यम् इति
2.15.57.m: Then, handing him the two churning-sticks, he says: "You will be keeping silence; give instructions for whatever you have to instruct."

2.15.57.s: sa āha brāhmaṇān āśayatāśvaṃ gopāyata saṃbhārān nidhatta | iti
2.15.57.d: स आह ब्राह्मणान् आशयताश्वं गोपायत संभारान् निधत्त । इति
2.15.57.m: He says: "Feed the brāhmaṇas, guard the horse, store up the materials."
His setting up of the fires is accompanied by abundance of food.

2.15.57.s: sāgnyādheyasya samṛddhis tad āhur nāgnyādheye gāṃ kurvīta ghorarūpam iti
2.15.57.d: साग्न्याधेयस्य समृद्धिस् तद् आहुर् नाग्न्याधेये गां कुर्वीत घोररूपम् इति
2.15.57.m: That is the success of the setting up of the fires. Regarding this they say: in the setting up of the fires one should not immolate a cow; it has a terrible form.

2.15.57.s: kurvītaivāpi tv eva na kurvīta | api bahvīr api kurvīta | anu caitasya bhavet puṇyā praśam̐seti kātyas |
2.15.57.d: कुर्वीतैवापि त्व् एव न कुर्वीत । अपि बह्वीर् अपि कुर्वीत । अनु चैतस्य भवेत् पुण्या प्रशँसेति कात्यस् ।
2.15.57.m: He may indeed do so, or he may not do so; he may even offer many; and an auspicious praise would attend him, so says Kātya.
Then he hands him the two churning-sticks.

2.15.57.s: te pratigṛhṇāti mahī viśpatnī sadane ṛtasyārvācī etaṃ dharuṇe rayīṇām | antarvatnī janyaṃ jātavedasam adhvarāṇāṃ janayathaḥ purogām || ārohataṃ daśatam̐ śakvarīr mamartvenāgna āyuṣā varcasā saha | jyog jīvanta uttarāmuttarām̐ samāṃ darśam ahaṃ pūrṇamāsaṃ yajñaṃ yathā yajai | iti |
2.15.57.d: ते प्रतिगृह्णाति मही विश्पत्नी सदने ऋतस्यार्वाची एतं धरुणे रयीणाम् । अन्तर्वत्नी जन्यं जातवेदसम् अध्वराणां जनयथः पुरोगाम् ॥ आरोहतं दशतँ शक्वरीर् ममर्त्वेनाग्न आयुषा वर्चसा सह । ज्योग् जीवन्त उत्तरामुत्तराँ समां दर्शम् अहं पूर्णमासं यज्ञं यथा यजै । इति ।
2.15.57.m: He receives them with: "The great mistress of the clan, in the seat of order, turned towards us, come in the supporter of riches! / Pregnant, you two give birth to the born-of-clans Jātavedas, the leader of the rites. / Mount the decade, the śakvarī verses, for me, O Agni, with truth, with life, with brilliance! / Living long, year after year, may I sacrifice the new-moon and the full-moon sacrifice!"

2.15.57.s: athaine upanigṛhṇāti | ṛtviyavatī stho agniretasau garbhaṃ dadhāthāṃ te vām ahaṃ dade | tat satyaṃ yad vīraṃ bibhṛtho vīraṃ janayiṣyathaḥ | te mat prātaḥ prajaniṣyethe te mā prajāte prajanayiṣyathaḥ | prajayā paśubhir brahmavarcasena suvarge loke | iti |
2.15.57.d: अथैने उपनिगृह्णाति । ऋत्वियवती स्थो अग्निरेतसौ गर्भं दधाथां ते वाम् अहं ददे । तत् सत्यं यद् वीरं बिभृथो वीरं जनयिष्यथः । ते मत् प्रातः प्रजनिष्येथे ते मा प्रजाते प्रजनयिष्यथः । प्रजया पशुभिर् ब्रह्मवर्चसेन सुवर्गे लोके । इति ।
2.15.57.m: Then he presses them down [to his chest]: "You two are in your season, having the seed of Agni; bear a fetus; as such, I take you both. / True is that you bear a hero, you will give birth to a hero. / From me you shall be born tomorrow morning; having been born, you shall bring me forth / with offspring, cattle, Vedic brilliance, in the heavenly world."

2.15.58.s: athainam anṛtāt satyam upanayati mānuṣād daivyam upanayati | idam aham anṛtāt satyam upaimi mānuṣād daivyam upaimi daivīṃ vācaṃ yacchāmi | iti
2.15.58.d: अथैनम् अनृतात् सत्यम् उपनयति मानुषाद् दैव्यम् उपनयति । इदम् अहम् अनृतात् सत्यम् उपैमि मानुषाद् दैव्यम् उपैमि दैवीं वाचं यच्छामि । इति
2.15.58.m: Then he leads him from falsehood to truth, he leads [him] from the human to the divine: "Here I enter from falsehood into truth; I enter from the human to the divine; I restrain divine speech."
Keeping silence, they sit keeping him awake during the night.

2.15.58.s: śalkais tām̐ rātrim agnim indhate śalkair agnim indhāna ubhau lokau sanem aham | ubhayor lokayor ṛdhvāti mṛtyuṃ tarāmy aham iti |
2.15.58.d: शल्कैस् ताँ रात्रिम् अग्निम् इन्धते शल्कैर् अग्निम् इन्धान उभौ लोकौ सनेम् अहम् । उभयोर् लोकयोर् ऋध्वाति मृत्युं तराम्य् अहम् इति ।
2.15.58.m: They kindle the fire through that night with wood splinters: "Kindling the fire with wood splinters, may I win both worlds; / thriving in both worlds, I cross beyond death."

2.15.58.s: uttareṇa gārhapatyasyāyatanaṃ kalmāṣam ajaṃ badhnāti tenainam ādhāsyamānam̐ saṃkhyāpayati prajā agne saṃvāsayāśāś ca paśubhiḥ saha | rāṣṭrāṇy asmā ādhehi yāny āsant savituḥ save | iti ||
2.15.58.d: उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यस्यायतनं कल्माषम् अजं बध्नाति तेनैनम् आधास्यमानँ संख्यापयति प्रजा अग्ने संवासयाशाश् च पशुभिः सह । राष्ट्राण्य् अस्मा आधेहि यान्य् आसन्त् सवितुः सवे । इति ॥
2.15.58.m: To the north of the fireplace of the gārhapatya he ties a spotted he-goat; with it he causes the one about to establish [the fires] to view [the hearth]: "Settle the offspring, O Agni, and the quarters together with cattle. / Bestow upon him the kingdoms that existed in the impulse of Savitar."

2.16.58.s: athādhvaryur apararātra ādrutyāraṇī niṣṭapati jātavedo bhuvanasya retas | iha siñca tapaso yaj janiṣyate | agnim aśvatthād adhi havyavāham | śamīgarbhāj janayan yo mayobhūḥ || ayaṃ te yonir ṛtviyas | yato jāto arocathāḥ | taṃ jānann agna āroha | āthā no vardhayā rayim iti |
2.16.58.d: अथाध्वर्युर् अपररात्र आद्रुत्यारणी निष्टपति जातवेदो भुवनस्य रेतस् । इह सिञ्च तपसो यज् जनिष्यते । अग्निम् अश्वत्थाद् अधि हव्यवाहम् । शमीगर्भाज् जनयन् यो मयोभूः ॥ अयं ते योनिर् ऋत्वियस् । यतो जातो अरोचथाः । तं जानन्न् अग्न आरोह । आथा नो वर्धया रयिम् इति ।
2.16.58.m: Then in the latter part of the night the adhvaryu priest runs up and heats the churning sticks over the fire: "O Jātavedas, the seed of the world, / pour here what will be born from heat: / bringing forth Agni, the bearer of oblations, from the aśvattha tree, / from the womb of the śamī tree, who is delightful. / This is your seasonal womb / from which, born, you shone. / Knowing it, O Agni, ascend [it], / and then increase our wealth."

2.16.58.s: athaitam agnim̐ sate samupya dakṣiṇato jvalayanta āsate |
2.16.58.d: अथैतम् अग्निँ सते समुप्य दक्षिणतो ज्वलयन्त आसते ।
2.16.58.m: Then, having gathered this fire in a shallow pan, they sit keeping it burning to the south.

2.16.59.s: athaitāny agnyāyatanāni śakṛtpiṇḍena parilepayati | atha tṛtīyam̐ saṃbhārāṇām ādāya gārhapatyasyāyatane nivapati yat pṛthivyā anāmṛtam̐ saṃbabhūva tve sacā | tad agnir agnaye 'dadāt tasminn ādhīyatām ayam iti
2.16.59.d: अथैतान्य् अग्न्यायतनानि शकृत्पिण्डेन परिलेपयति । अथ तृतीयँ संभाराणाम् आदाय गार्हपत्यस्यायतने निवपति यत् पृथिव्या अनामृतँ संबभूव त्वे सचा । तद् अग्निर् अग्नये ऽददात् तस्मिन्न् आधीयताम् अयम् इति
2.16.59.m: Then he smears these fire hearths around with a ball of cow dung. / Then, taking a third of the materials, he scatters them in the fireplace of the gārhapatya: "What non-mortal [substance] of the earth arose together in you, / that Agni gave to Agni; in that let this [fire] be established."

2.16.59.s: sa yatroṣān upādhigacchati taj japati yad adaś candramasi kṛṣṇaṃ tad apīha | iti |
2.16.59.d: स यत्रोषान् उपाधिगच्छति तज् जपति यद् अदश् चन्द्रमसि कृष्णं तद् अपीह । इति ।
2.16.59.m: When he comes upon the saline earth, he mutters then: "What is black over there in the moon, that too is here."

2.16.59.s: athainān ādadhāti divas tvā vīryeṇa pṛthivyai mahimnā | antarikṣasya poṣeṇa sarvapaśum ādadhe | iti |
2.16.59.d: अथैनान् आदधाति दिवस् त्वा वीर्येण पृथिव्यै महिम्ना । अन्तरिक्षस्य पोषेण सर्वपशुम् आदधे । इति ।
2.16.59.m: Then he establishes them: "By the vigor of heaven, by the greatness of earth, / by the nourishment of the intermediate space, I establish you possessing all cattle."

2.16.59.s: athainān saṃprayauti saṃ vaḥ sṛjāmi hṛdayāni sam̐sṛṣṭaṃ mano astu vaḥ | sam̐sṛṣṭhaḥ prāṇo astu vaḥ || saṃ yā vaḥ priyās tanuvaḥ saṃpriyā hṛdayāni vaḥ | ātmā vo astu saṃpriyaḥ saṃpriyās tanuvo mama | iti |
2.16.59.d: अथैनान् संप्रयौति सं वः सृजामि हृदयानि सँसृष्टं मनो अस्तु वः । सँसृष्ठः प्राणो अस्तु वः ॥ सं या वः प्रियास् तनुवः संप्रिया हृदयानि वः । आत्मा वो अस्तु संप्रियः संप्रियास् तनुवो मम । इति ।
2.16.59.m: Then he mixes them together: "I unite your hearts; united let your mind be; / united let your breath be. / Those bodies of yours that are dear, may they be dear together, dear together your hearts. / May your self be dear together, dear together my bodies."

2.16.59.s: athainān kalpayati kalpetāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī kalpantām āpa oṣadhīḥ | kalpantām agnayaḥ pṛthaṅ mama jyaiṣṭhyāya savratāḥ || ye 'gnayaḥ samanaso 'ntarā dyāvāpṛthivī | vāsantikāvṛtū abhi kalpamānā indram iva devā abhisaṃviśantu | iti |
2.16.59.d: अथैनान् कल्पयति कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्ताम् आप ओषधीः । कल्पन्ताम् अग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः ॥ ये ऽग्नयः समनसो ऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवी । वासन्तिकावृतू अभि कल्पमाना इन्द्रम् इव देवा अभिसंविशन्तु । इति ।
2.16.59.m: Then he arranges them: "May heaven and earth be arranged; may waters and plants be arranged. / May the fires, observing the same vow, be arranged separately for my seniority. / Which fires of one mind are between heaven and earth, / being arranged toward the two spring seasons, like the gods toward Indra, let them enter together."

2.16.59.s: athātiśiṣṭānām̐ saṃbhārāṇām ardhān ādāya dakṣiṇayā dvāropanirhṛtyānvāhāryapacanasyāyatane nivapati yad antarikṣasyānāmṛtam̐ saṃbabhūva tve sacā | tad vāyur agnaye 'dādāt tasminn ādhīyatām ayam iti
2.16.59.d: अथातिशिष्टानाँ संभाराणाम् अर्धान् आदाय दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्यान्वाहार्यपचनस्यायतने निवपति यद् अन्तरिक्षस्यानामृतँ संबभूव त्वे सचा । तद् वायुर् अग्नये ऽदादात् तस्मिन्न् आधीयताम् अयम् इति
2.16.59.m: Then, taking half of the remaining materials, carrying them out through the south door, he scatters them in the fireplace of the anvāhāryapacana: "What non-mortal [substance] of the intermediate space arose together in you, / that Vāyu gave to Agni; in that let this [fire] be established."

2.16.59.s: sa yatroṣān upādhigacchati taj japati yad adaś candramasi kṛṣṇaṃ tad apīha | iti
2.16.59.d: स यत्रोषान् उपाधिगच्छति तज् जपति यद् अदश् चन्द्रमसि कृष्णं तद् अपीह । इति
2.16.59.m: When he comes upon the saline earth, he mutters then: "What is black over there in the moon, that too is here."

2.16.59.s: tathādadhāti tathā saṃprayauti tathā kalpayati | athaitenaiva yathetam etyātiśiṣṭān saṃbhārān ādāya pūrvayā dvāropanirhṛtyāhavanīyasyāyatane nivapati yad divo 'nāmṛtam̐ saṃbabhūva tve sacā tad ādityo 'gnaye 'dadāt tasminn ādhīyatām ayam iti
2.16.59.d: तथादधाति तथा संप्रयौति तथा कल्पयति । अथैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्यातिशिष्टान् संभारान् आदाय पूर्वया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्याहवनीयस्यायतने निवपति यद् दिवो ऽनामृतँ संबभूव त्वे सचा तद् आदित्यो ऽग्नये ऽददात् तस्मिन्न् आधीयताम् अयम् इति
2.16.59.m: In the same manner he establishes; / in the same manner he mixes together; / in the same manner he arranges. / Then, having gone back precisely the way he went, taking the remaining materials, carrying them out through the eastern door, he scatters them in the fireplace of the āhavanīya: "What non-mortal [substance] of heaven arose together in you, / that Āditya gave to Agni; in that let this [fire] be established."

2.16.59.s: sa yatroṣān upādhigacchati taj japati yad adaś candramasi kṛṣṇaṃ tad apīha | iti
2.16.59.d: स यत्रोषान् उपाधिगच्छति तज् जपति यद् अदश् चन्द्रमसि कृष्णं तद् अपीह । इति
2.16.59.m: When he comes upon the saline earth, he mutters then: "What is black over there in the moon, that too is here."

2.16.60.m: In the same manner he establishes; / in the same manner he mixes together; / in the same manner he arranges.

2.16.60.s: sa āha vihṛtā agnayo mā kaś canāntareṇa saṃcārīt | iti |
2.16.60.d: स आह विहृता अग्नयो मा कश् चनान्तरेण संचारीत् । इति ।
2.16.60.m: He says: "The fires have been separated; let no one walk in between."

2.16.60.s: athādhvaryuḥ pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya pratyaṅṅ ādrutya gārhapatyasyāyatana upari saṃbhāreṣu muñjakulāyaṃ nidadhāti
2.16.60.d: अथाध्वर्युः प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य प्रत्यङ्ङ् आद्रुत्य गार्हपत्यस्यायतन उपरि संभारेषु मुञ्जकुलायं निदधाति
2.16.60.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, having turned from left to right, running toward the west, places a nest of muñja grass upon the materials in the fireplace of the gārhapatya.

2.16.60.s: tasmin pratīcīnaprajananām araṇiṃ nidhāya daśahotrottarāraṇim avadadhāti
2.16.60.d: तस्मिन् प्रतीचीनप्रजननाम् अरणिं निधाय दशहोत्रोत्तरारणिम् अवदधाति
2.16.60.m: Having laid down the lower churning stick with its socket turned westward in it, he puts down the upper churning stick with the Daśahotṛ formula.

2.16.60.s: sa āha manthata | iti yajamānaḥ prathamo manthati yajamāna uttamo manthati
2.16.60.d: स आह मन्थत । इति यजमानः प्रथमो मन्थति यजमान उत्तमो मन्थति
2.16.60.m: He says: "Churn!" / The sacrificer churns first; / the sacrificer churns last.

2.16.60.s: janayati jāte varaṃ dadāmi | iti vācaṃ visṛjate |
2.16.60.d: जनयति जाते वरं ददामि । इति वाचं विसृजते ।
2.16.60.m: He generates [fire]. / When it is born, he releases his speech with: "I give a boon."

2.16.60.s: athainam upatiṣṭhate | ajījanann amṛtaṃ martyāsas | asremāṇaṃ taraṇiṃ vīḍujambham | daśa svasāro agruvaḥ samīcīḥ pumām̐saṃ jātam abhisam̐rabhantām iti |
2.16.60.d: अथैनम् उपतिष्ठते । अजीजनन्न् अमृतं मर्त्यासस् । अस्रेमाणं तरणिं वीडुजम्भम् । दश स्वसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमाँसं जातम् अभिसँरभन्ताम् इति ।
2.16.60.m: Then he attends upon it: "Mortals have generated the immortal, / the untiring, the swift, with strong teeth. / Let the ten maiden sisters together / take hold of the born male."

2.16.60.s: athainam abhiprāṇiti prajāpates tvā prāṇenābhiprāṇimi pūṣṇaḥ poṣeṇa mahyam | dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya śatam̐ śaradbhya āyuṣe varcase jīvātvai puṇyāya || prāṇe tvāmṛtam ādadhāmy annādam annādyāya goptāraṃ guptyai | iti |
2.16.60.d: अथैनम् अभिप्राणिति प्रजापतेस् त्वा प्राणेनाभिप्राणिमि पूष्णः पोषेण मह्यम् । दीर्घायुत्वाय शतशारदाय शतँ शरद्भ्य आयुषे वर्चसे जीवात्वै पुण्याय ॥ प्राणे त्वामृतम् आदधाम्य् अन्नादम् अन्नाद्याय गोप्तारं गुप्त्यै । इति ।
2.16.60.m: Then he breathes upon it: "With the breath of Prajāpati I breathe upon you, with the nourishment of Pūṣan, for myself, / for long life of a hundred autumns, for a life of a hundred autumns, for vigor, for living, for merit. / In your breath I place immortality, the eater of food for food-eating, the guardian for protection."
Then he says to the udgātṛ priest: "Chant the rathaṃtara saman."

2.16.60.s: athainam ādadhāti bhūr bhuvas | gharmaḥ śiras tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhuvat | chardistokāya tanayāya yaccha || bhṛgūṇāṃ tvāṅgirasāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti bhṛgvaṅgirasām ādadhyāt |
2.16.60.d: अथैनम् आदधाति भूर् भुवस् । घर्मः शिरस् तद् अयम् अग्निः संप्रियः पशुभिर् भुवत् । छर्दिस्तोकाय तनयाय यच्छ ॥ भृगूणां त्वाङ्गिरसां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति भृग्वङ्गिरसाम् आदध्यात् ।
2.16.60.m: Then he establishes it: / "Bhūr, bhuvaḥ! / The gharma is the head. So may this Agni be dear together with the cattle; / give shelter to the child, to the offspring." / "For the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases he should establish with: 'By the vow of the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases, O lord of vows, I establish you.'"

2.16.60.s: ādityānāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmi | ity anyāsāṃ brāhmaṇīnāṃ prajānām | varuṇasya tvā rājño vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti rājñas |
2.16.60.d: आदित्यानां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इत्य् अन्यासां ब्राह्मणीनां प्रजानाम् । वरुणस्य त्वा राज्ञो व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति राज्ञस् ।
2.16.60.m: "'By the vow of the Āditya gods, O lord of vows, I establish you,' for the other brāhmaṇa people; / 'By the vow of King Varuṇa, O lord of vows, I establish you,' for a king;"

2.16.60.s: indrasya tvendriyeṇa vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti rājanyasya
2.16.60.d: इन्द्रस्य त्वेन्द्रियेण व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति राजन्यस्य
2.16.60.m: "'By the power of Indra, O lord of vows, I establish you,' for a rājanya;"

2.16.60.s: manos tvā grāmaṇyo vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti vaiśyasya
2.16.60.d: मनोस् त्वा ग्रामण्यो व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति वैश्यस्य
2.16.60.m: "'By the vow of Manu the village-headman, O lord of vows, I establish you,' for a vaiśya;"

2.16.61.s: ṛbhūṇāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti rathakārasya | iti
2.16.61.d: ऋभूणां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति रथकारस्य । इति
2.16.61.m: "'By the vow of the Ṛbhu gods, O lord of vows, I establish you,' for a chariot-maker."
According to the seer, according to the lineage: / "with the gāyatrī meter."

2.16.61.s: uttarato hiraṇyaśalkam upāsyati svayā tanuvā saṃbhava | iti | athaitam̐ rājataṃ vṛṣalāya vājñātāya vātiprayacchati |
2.16.61.d: उत्तरतो हिरण्यशल्कम् उपास्यति स्वया तनुवा संभव । इति । अथैतँ राजतं वृषलाय वाज्ञाताय वातिप्रयच्छति ।
2.16.61.m: To the north he throws a splinter of gold, saying: "Unite with your own body." / Then he passes on this silver piece to a śūdra or to an unknown person.
"It is distress that he thus passes on," says the brāhmaṇa passage.

2.16.61.s: athainam upatiṣṭhate ahaṃ tvad asmi mad asi tvam etat | mamāsi yonis tava yonir asmi | mamaiva sanvaha havyāny agne putraḥ pitre lokakṛjjātavedaḥ || sugārhapatyo vidahann arātīs | uṣasaḥ śreyasīḥśreyasīr dadhat | agne sapatnām̐ apabādhamānas | rāyaspoṣam iṣam ūrjam asmāsu dhehi | iti ||
2.16.61.d: अथैनम् उपतिष्ठते अहं त्वद् अस्मि मद् असि त्वम् एतत् । ममासि योनिस् तव योनिर् अस्मि । ममैव सन्वह हव्यान्य् अग्ने पुत्रः पित्रे लोककृज्जातवेदः ॥ सुगार्हपत्यो विदहन्न् अरातीस् । उषसः श्रेयसीःश्रेयसीर् दधत् । अग्ने सपत्नाँ अपबाधमानस् । रायस्पोषम् इषम् ऊर्जम् अस्मासु धेहि । इति ॥
2.16.61.m: Then he attends upon it with: "I am from you, you are from me in this; / you are my origin, I am your origin. / Being mine indeed, carry the oblations, O Agni, / a son to a father, preparing the world, O Jātavedas! / Possessing a good gārhapatya, burning away enemies, / bringing ever better dawns, / O Agni, beating back adversaries, / place in us abundance of wealth, refreshment, and vigor!"

2.17.61.s: athaitam agnim ādadate ya eṣa sate samupto bhavati taṃ dakṣiṇayā dvāropanirhṛtyānvāhāryapacanam ādadhāti bhūr bhuvas | vātaḥ prāṇas tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhuvat | svaditaṃ tokāya tanayāya pituṃ paca || amīṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti
2.17.61.d: अथैतम् अग्निम् आददते य एष सते समुप्तो भवति तं दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिर्हृत्यान्वाहार्यपचनम् आदधाति भूर् भुवस् । वातः प्राणस् तद् अयम् अग्निः संप्रियः पशुभिर् भुवत् । स्वदितं तोकाय तनयाय पितुं पच ॥ अमीषां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति
2.17.61.m: Then they take that fire which was gathered into the pan. Having carried it out through the southern door, he sets up the anvāhāryapacana fire with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ! Wind is breath; therefore let this Agni be pleasing along with the cattle! Cook well-tasted food for offspring and descendants! Lord of vows, I set you up with the vow of these gods:"

2.17.61.s: yatharṣi yathāgotram | gāyatreṇa chandasā | iti | uttarato hiraṇyaśalkamupāsyati svayā tanuvā saṃbhaveti |
2.17.61.d: यथर्षि यथागोत्रम् । गायत्रेण छन्दसा । इति । उत्तरतो हिरण्यशल्कमुपास्यति स्वया तनुवा संभवेति ।
2.17.61.m: according to the seer, according to the lineage, with: "by the gāyatrī metre." On the north side he throws down a gold chip with: "Unite with your own body!"
Then he hands over that silver [piece] to a Śūdra or to a stranger.
"He hands over misfortune itself," says the brāhmaṇa passage.

2.17.61.s: api vā gārhapatyād evānvāhāryapacanam ādadhāti prajāpatir agnim asṛjata so 'bibhet pra mā dhakṣyatīti tasya tredhā mahimānaṃ vyauhac chāntyā apradāhāya | ity etasmād brāhmaṇāt |
2.17.61.d: अपि वा गार्हपत्याद् एवान्वाहार्यपचनम् आदधाति प्रजापतिर् अग्निम् असृजत सो ऽबिभेत् प्र मा धक्ष्यतीति तस्य त्रेधा महिमानं व्यौहच् छान्त्या अप्रदाहाय । इत्य् एतस्माद् ब्राह्मणात् ।
2.17.61.m: Or rather, he sets up the anvāhāryapacana fire from the gārhapatya fire itself, on account of this brāhmaṇa passage: "Prajāpati created Agni; he feared: 'He will burn me up.' He spread his greatness threefold for appeasement, that he might not burn."

2.17.61.s: athainam upatiṣṭhate | imā u mām upatiṣṭhantu rāya ābhiḥ prajābhir iha saṃvaseya | iho iḍā tiṣṭhatu viśvarūpī madhye vasor dīdihi jātavedas | iti |
2.17.61.d: अथैनम् उपतिष्ठते । इमा उ माम् उपतिष्ठन्तु राय आभिः प्रजाभिर् इह संवसेय । इहो इडा तिष्ठतु विश्वरूपी मध्ये वसोर् दीदिहि जातवेदस् । इति ।
2.17.61.m: Then he attends upon it with: "May these riches attend upon me; may I dwell here with these offspring! May Iḍā abide here, having every form; shine in the midst of wealth, O Jātavedas!"

2.17.61.s: athaitenaiva yathetam etyābhyādadhātīdhmaṃ praṇayanīyam | taṃ tathābhyādadhāti yathā manyate 'rdhodite sūrya āhavanīya ādhīyamānaḥ saṃpatsyata iti
2.17.61.d: अथैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्याभ्यादधातीध्मं प्रणयनीयम् । तं तथाभ्यादधाति यथा मन्यते ऽर्धोदिते सूर्य आहवनीय आधीयमानः संपत्स्यत इति
2.17.61.m: Then, having returned by the very way he had gone, he places the kindling wood for the forward conveyance [on the fire]. He places it in such a way that he thinks: "When the sun is half-risen, the āhavanīya fire being set up will be accomplished."

2.17.62.m: It turns out for him accordingly. They prepare the supporting firewood sticks.

2.17.62.s: aśva eṣa pūrvavāṭ palpūlitaḥ purastāt tiṣṭhati |
2.17.62.d: अश्व एष पूर्ववाट् पल्पूलितः पुरस्तात् तिष्ठति ।
2.17.62.m: This horse, an experienced draft-horse, bathed, stands in front.

2.17.62.s: athainam udyacchate | ojase balāya tvodyacche vṛṣaṇe śuṣmāyāyuṣe varcase | sapatnatūr asi vṛtratūḥ || yas te deveṣu mahimā suvargo yas ta ātmā paśuṣu pravṣṭaḥ | puṣṭir yā te manuṣyeṣu paprathe tayā no agne juṣamāṇa ehi || divaḥ pṛthivyāḥ pary antarikṣād vātāt paśubhyo adhyoṣadhībhyaḥ | yatrayatra jātavedaḥ saṃbabhūtha tato no agne juṣamāṇa ehi | iti |
2.17.62.d: अथैनम् उद्यच्छते । ओजसे बलाय त्वोद्यच्छे वृषणे शुष्मायायुषे वर्चसे । सपत्नतूर् असि वृत्रतूः ॥ यस् ते देवेषु महिमा सुवर्गो यस् त आत्मा पशुषु प्रव्ष्टः । पुष्टिर् या ते मनुष्येषु पप्रथे तया नो अग्ने जुषमाण एहि ॥ दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्य् अन्तरिक्षाद् वातात् पशुभ्यो अध्योषधीभ्यः । यत्रयत्र जातवेदः संबभूथ ततो नो अग्ने जुषमाण एहि । इति ।
2.17.62.m: Then he lifts it up with: "For vitality, for strength I lift you up, for the bull, for vigor, for life, for splendor! You are an expeller of rivals, an expeller of Vṛtra. The heavenly greatness of yours that is among the gods, the self of yours that entered into cattle, the nourishment of yours that spread among men—with that, O Agni, come graciously to us! From the sky, from the earth, from the intermediate space, from the wind, from the cattle, from the plants—from wherever you arose, O Jātavedas, come from there graciously to us, O Agni!"

2.17.62.s: atheyati | atheyati | adho'dhaḥ śiro harati | iti brāhmaṇam ādadāna evaitā mātrā abhisaṃpādayed ity etad aparam
2.17.62.d: अथेयति । अथेयति । अधोऽधः शिरो हरति । इति ब्राह्मणम् आददान एवैता मात्रा अभिसंपादयेद् इत्य् एतद् अपरम्
2.17.62.m: then at this [height]; then at this [height]. "He carries it below the head," says the brāhmaṇa passage. Another [view] is that he should accomplish these measures just while taking it.

2.17.62.s: tam anumantrayate prācīm anu pradiśaṃ prehi vidvān agner agne puro agnir bhaveha | viśvā āśā dīdyāno vibhāhy ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade catuṣpade | iti
2.17.62.d: तम् अनुमन्त्रयते प्राचीम् अनु प्रदिशं प्रेहि विद्वान् अग्नेर् अग्ने पुरो अग्निर् भवेह । विश्वा आशा दीद्यानो विभाह्य् ऊर्जं नो धेहि द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । इति
2.17.62.m: He addresses it with: "Go forward along the eastern direction, knowing [the way]! O Agni, become the lead-fire of Agni here! Shining, illuminate all directions; grant us vigor for two-footed and four-footed [beings]!"

2.17.62.s: viṣuvaty uparamanti vikramasva mahām̐ asi vediṣan mānuṣebhyas triṣu lokeṣu jāgṛhi | iti |
2.17.62.d: विषुवत्य् उपरमन्ति विक्रमस्व महाँ असि वेदिषन् मानुषेभ्यस् त्रिषु लोकेषु जागृहि । इति ।
2.17.62.m: At the halfway point they stop with: "Stride forth, you are great; being an altar-sitter for men, be watchful in the three worlds!"

2.17.62.s: athopātiyanti | anv agnir uṣasām agram akhyad anv ahāni prathamo jātavedāḥ | anu sūryasya purutrā ca raśmīn anu dyāvāpṛthivī ātatāna | iti |
2.17.62.d: अथोपातियन्ति । अन्व् अग्निर् उषसाम् अग्रम् अख्यद् अन्व् अहानि प्रथमो जातवेदाः । अनु सूर्यस्य पुरुत्रा च रश्मीन् अनु द्यावापृथिवी आततान । इति ।
2.17.62.m: Then they move past with: "Agni has looked after the start of the dawns, first Jātavedas after the days; after the many rays of the sun, and he has extended after heaven and earth."

2.17.62.s: athaitenāśvena prācottarataḥ pārśvataḥ saṃbhārāṇām ākramayati yathāhitasyāgner aṅgārā abhyavavarterann iti |
2.17.62.d: अथैतेनाश्वेन प्राचोत्तरतः पार्श्वतः संभाराणाम् आक्रमयति यथाहितस्याग्नेर् अङ्गारा अभ्यववर्तेरन्न् इति ।
2.17.62.m: Then, with this horse, he makes [it] step on the north-east side of the ritual equipment so that the embers of the established fire might roll towards it.
Then, having turned it clockwise and sprinkled it with water, he releases it toward the north.

2.17.62.s: sa eṣo 'dhvaryor bhavati | anyaṃ brahmaṇe dadāti | atha pradakṣiṇam āvṛtyedhmaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati yad idaṃ divo yad adaḥ pṛthivyāḥ saṃvidāne rodasī saṃbabhūvatuḥ | tayoḥ pṛṣṭhe sīdatu jātavedāḥ śambhūḥ prajābhyas tanuve syonaḥ || prāṇaṃ tvām ṛta ādadhāmy annādam annādyāya goptāraṃ guptyai | iti |
2.17.62.d: स एषो ऽध्वर्योर् भवति । अन्यं ब्रह्मणे ददाति । अथ प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्येध्मं प्रतिष्ठापयति यद् इदं दिवो यद् अदः पृथिव्याः संविदाने रोदसी संबभूवतुः । तयोः पृष्ठे सीदतु जातवेदाः शम्भूः प्रजाभ्यस् तनुवे स्योनः ॥ प्राणं त्वाम् ऋत आदधाम्य् अन्नादम् अन्नाद्याय गोप्तारं गुप्त्यै । इति ।
2.17.62.m: That [horse] belongs to the adhvaryu priest. He gives another to the brahman priest. Then, having turned clockwise, he sets down the kindling wood with: "What [was born] here of heaven, what there of earth, when the two worlds came together in agreement—upon their back let Jātavedas sit, bringing welfare to offspring, comfortable to the body! I establish you in Ṛta as breath, as the food-eater for eating food, as protector for protection."

2.17.63.s: athodgātāram āha bṛhad vāravantīyam̐ śyaitam iti gāya | iti
2.17.63.d: अथोद्गातारम् आह बृहद् वारवन्तीयँ श्यैतम् इति गाय । इति
2.17.63.m: Then he says to the udgātṛ priest: "Sing the Bṛhat, the Vāravantīya, and the Śyaita [samans]!"

2.17.63.s: sarvāṇi saṃpreṣyati bṛhati gīyamāna āhavanīyam ādadhāti bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar arkaś cakṣus tad asau sūryas tad ayam agniḥ saṃpriyaḥ paśubhir bhuvat | yat te śukra śukraṃ varcaḥ śukrā tanūḥ śukraṃ jyotir ajasraṃ tena me dīdihi tena tvādadhe 'gnināgne brahmaṇā amīṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmi | iti
2.17.63.d: सर्वाणि संप्रेष्यति बृहति गीयमान आहवनीयम् आदधाति भूर् भुवः सुवर् अर्कश् चक्षुस् तद् असौ सूर्यस् तद् अयम् अग्निः संप्रियः पशुभिर् भुवत् । यत् ते शुक्र शुक्रं वर्चः शुक्रा तनूः शुक्रं ज्योतिर् अजस्रं तेन मे दीदिहि तेन त्वादधे ऽग्निनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा अमीषां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामि । इति
2.17.63.m: He gives all the summonses. While the Bṛhat is being sung, he sets up the āhavanīya fire with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar! The sun-beam is the eye, that sun yonder is that, so let this Agni be pleasing along with the cattle! O bright one, what bright brilliance, bright body, bright unceasing light is yours, shine upon me with that; with that fire, with holy power, O Agni, I set you up! Lord of vows, I set you up with the vow of these gods:"

2.17.63.s: yatharṣi yathāgotram | gāyatreṇa chandasā | iti | uttarato hiraṇyaśalkam upāsyati svayā tanuvā saṃbhava | iti |
2.17.63.d: यथर्षि यथागोत्रम् । गायत्रेण छन्दसा । इति । उत्तरतो हिरण्यशल्कम् उपास्यति स्वया तनुवा संभव । इति ।
2.17.63.m: according to the seer, according to the lineage, with: "by the gāyatrī metre." On the north side he throws down a gold chip with: "Unite with your own body!"
Then he hands over that silver [piece] to a Śūdra or to a stranger.

2.17.63.s: ārtim evātiprayacchati | iti brāhmaṇam athainam upatiṣṭhate | ānaśe vyānaśe sarvam āyur vyānaśe | iti |
2.17.63.d: आर्तिम् एवातिप्रयच्छति । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथैनम् उपतिष्ठते । आनशे व्यानशे सर्वम् आयुर् व्यानशे । इति ।
2.17.63.m: "He hands over misfortune itself," says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then he attends upon it with: "I have reached, I have pervaded, I have pervaded the whole lifespan!"

2.17.63.s: atraitāv agnī ādadhāti sabhyaṃ cāvasathīyaṃ ca
2.17.63.d: अत्रैताव् अग्नी आदधाति सभ्यं चावसथीयं च
2.17.63.m: At this point he sets up these two fires: the sabhya and the āvasathīya.
He rolls a chariot wheel continuously from the gārhapatya fire to the āhavanīya fire.

2.18.63.s: sarvauṣadhena vyāhṛtībhir agnīñ chamayitvā pañcapañca nānāvṛkṣyāḥ samidho 'bhyajyābhidadhāti samidhyamānaḥ prathamo nu dharmas | ity etābhiḥ pañcabhis | āyurdā agne haviṣo juṣāṇas | ity etām apoddhṛtya |
2.18.63.d: सर्वौषधेन व्याहृतीभिर् अग्नीञ् छमयित्वा पञ्चपञ्च नानावृक्ष्याः समिधो ऽभ्यज्याभिदधाति समिध्यमानः प्रथमो नु धर्मस् । इत्य् एताभिः पञ्चभिस् । आयुर्दा अग्ने हविषो जुषाणस् । इत्य् एताम् अपोद्धृत्य ।
2.18.63.m: Having appeased the fires with all kinds of herbs along with the sacred utterances, having anointed five kindling sticks from various trees for each [fire], he places them [on the fires] with these five [verses]: "Being kindled, first now the religious duty…", having set aside that [verse]: "O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation…"

2.18.64.s: atha pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya pratyaṅṅ ādrutya jaghanena gārhapatyaṃ tiṣṭham̐s tanūbhir upatiṣṭhate ye te agne śive tanuvau virāṭ ca svarāṭ ca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām | ye te agne śive tanuvau samrāṭ cābhibhūś ca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām | ye te agne śive tanuvau vibhūś ca paribhūś ca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām | ye te agne śive tanuvau prabhvī ca prabhūtiś ca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām | yās te agne śivās tanuvas tābhis tvādadhe | iti
2.18.64.d: अथ प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य प्रत्यङ्ङ् आद्रुत्य जघनेन गार्हपत्यं तिष्ठँस् तनूभिर् उपतिष्ठते ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ विराट् च स्वराट् च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् । ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ सम्राट् चाभिभूश् च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् । ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ विभूश् च परिभूश् च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् । ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ प्रभ्वी च प्रभूतिश् च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् । यास् ते अग्ने शिवास् तनुवस् ताभिस् त्वादधे । इति
2.18.64.m: Then, having turned clockwise and run westward, standing behind the gārhapatya fire, he attends upon [it] with the bodies [formula]: "The two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, which are the Virāj and the Svarāj, may they enter me, may they quicken me! The two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, which are the Samrāj and the Abhibhū, may they enter me, may they quicken me! The two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, which are the Vibhū and the Paribhū, may they enter me, may they quicken me! The two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, which are the Prabhvī and the Prabhūti, may they enter me, may they quicken me! With those which are your auspicious bodies, O Agni, with them I set you up!"
with all of them [he attends upon] the gārhapatya fire; with all of them the anvāhāryapacana fire;

2.18.64.s: sarvābhir āhavanīyam atha ghorās tanūr anudiśati yās te agne ghorās tanuvas tābhir amuṃ gaccha | iti |
2.18.64.d: सर्वाभिर् आहवनीयम् अथ घोरास् तनूर् अनुदिशति यास् ते अग्ने घोरास् तनुवस् ताभिर् अमुं गच्छ । इति ।
2.18.64.m: with all of them the āhavanīya fire. Then he points to the terrible bodies with: "Those which are your terrible bodies, O Agni, go with them against that one!"

2.18.64.s: atra yaṃ yajamāno dveṣṭi taṃ manasā dhyāyati |
2.18.64.d: अत्र यं यजमानो द्वेष्टि तं मनसा ध्यायति ।
2.18.64.m: At this point, whomever the sacrificer hates, he meditates upon him in his mind.

2.18.64.s: athāpa upaspṛśya virājakramair upatiṣṭhate narya prajāṃ me gopāya | amṛtatvāya jīvase | jātāṃ janiṣyamāṇāṃ ca | amṛte satye pratiṣṭhitām iti gārhapatyam
2.18.64.d: अथाप उपस्पृश्य विराजक्रमैर् उपतिष्ठते नर्य प्रजां मे गोपाय । अमृतत्वाय जीवसे । जातां जनिष्यमाणां च । अमृते सत्ये प्रतिष्ठिताम् इति गार्हपत्यम्
2.18.64.m: Then, having touched water, he worships [the fires] with the Virāj strides: "O Narya, protect my offspring, for immortality, for life, born and to be born, established in immortal truth"—[thus he addresses] the gārhapatya fire;

2.18.64.s: atharva pituṃ me gopāya | rasam annam ihāyuṣe | adabdhāyo 'śītatano | aviṣan naḥ pituṃ kṛṇu | ity anvāhāryapacanam |
2.18.64.d: अथर्व पितुं मे गोपाय । रसम् अन्नम् इहायुषे । अदब्धायो ऽशीततनो । अविषन् नः पितुं कृणु । इत्य् अन्वाहार्यपचनम् ।
2.18.64.m: "O Atharvan, protect my food, sap and sustenance here for life; of undeceived life, of uncold body, make our food unpoisonous"—thus the anvāhāryapacana fire;

2.18.64.s: śam̐sya paśūn me gopāya | dvipādo ye catuṣpadaḥ | aṣṭāśaphāś ca ya ihāgne | ye caikaśaphā āśugās | ity āhavanīyam |
2.18.64.d: शँस्य पशून् मे गोपाय । द्विपादो ये चतुष्पदः । अष्टाशफाश् च य इहाग्ने । ये चैकशफा आशुगास् । इत्य् आहवनीयम् ।
2.18.64.m: "O Śaṃsya, protect my livestock, two-footed and four-footed, and eight-hoofed here, O Agni, and one-hoofed swift runners"—thus the āhavanīya fire;

2.18.64.s: sapratha sabhāṃ me gopāya | ye ca sabhyāḥ sabhāsadaḥ | tān indriyāvataḥ kuru | sarvam āyur upāsatām iti sabhyam
2.18.64.d: सप्रथ सभां मे गोपाय । ये च सभ्याः सभासदः । तान् इन्द्रियावतः कुरु । सर्वम् आयुर् उपासताम् इति सभ्यम्
2.18.64.m: "O Saprathas, protect my assembly, and the assemblymen who sit in the assembly; make them endowed with vigor; let them attend their full lifespan"—thus the sabhya fire;

2.18.64.s: ahe budhniya mantraṃ me gopāya | yam ṛṣayas trayividā viduḥ | ṛcaḥ sāmāni yajūm̐ṣi | sā hi śrīr amṛtā satām ity āvasathīyam
2.18.64.d: अहे बुध्निय मन्त्रं मे गोपाय । यम् ऋषयस् त्रयिविदा विदुः । ऋचः सामानि यजूँषि । सा हि श्रीर् अमृता सताम् इत्य् आवसथीयम्
2.18.64.m: "O Ahi Budhnya, protect my sacred formula, which the seers knowing the three [Vedas] know, the ṛc, the saman, the yajus verses; for that is the immortal fortune of the good"—thus the āvasathīya fire;

2.18.65.s: atha gārhapatya ājyaṃ vilāpyotpūya sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā samidvaty āhavanīye pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvās | iti
2.18.65.d: अथ गार्हपत्य आज्यं विलाप्योत्पूय स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा समिद्वत्य् आहवनीये पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वास् । इति
2.18.65.m: Then, having melted ghee over the gārhapatya fire and purified it, having taken four ladlings in the ladle, he offers the full offering into the āhavanīya fire when it has kindling sticks, with: "Seven are your kindling sticks, O Agni, seven tongues…"

2.18.65.s: pūrṇāhutau varaṃ dadāti | athaitāny agnihotrapātrāṇi prakṣālitāny uttareṇa gārhapatyam upasādayati kūrce vā sūnāyāṃ vā sthālīm̐ sasruvām̐ srucam abhidyotanam̐ samidham iti |
2.18.65.d: पूर्णाहुतौ वरं ददाति । अथैतान्य् अग्निहोत्रपात्राणि प्रक्षालितान्य् उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यम् उपसादयति कूर्चे वा सूनायां वा स्थालीँ सस्रुवाँ स्रुचम् अभिद्योतनँ समिधम् इति ।
2.18.65.m: At the full offering he gives a boon. Then he sets down these washed agnihotra vessels north of the gārhapatya fire on a grass cushion or in a basket: the pot, the ladle along with the sruva, the brand, and the kindling stick.

2.18.65.s: athaitām agnihotrīṃ dakṣiṇata udīcīm̐ sthāpayitvā brāhmaṇo dogdhi
2.18.65.d: अथैताम् अग्निहोत्रीं दक्षिणत उदीचीँ स्थापयित्वा ब्राह्मणो दोग्धि
2.18.65.m: Then, having made this agnihotra cow stand south facing north, a brahmin milks her.

2.18.65.s: pūrvau duhyāt | aparau duhyāt | na saṃmṛśet | dvayor duhyāt paśukāmasya | iti |
2.18.65.d: पूर्वौ दुह्यात् । अपरौ दुह्यात् । न संमृशेत् । द्वयोर् दुह्यात् पशुकामस्य । इति ।
2.18.65.m: He should milk the two front [teats]; he should milk the two hind [teats]; he should not touch [them together]; "He should milk two for one desiring cattle," so [says] the scripture.

2.18.65.s: adhiśrityottaram ānayati | athaitad agnihotram agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya pūrvayā dvārā prapādya jaghanena gārhapatyam upasādya tasminn agnihotravidhiṃ ceṣṭitvā samidham upayatya prāṅ harati
2.18.65.d: अधिश्रित्योत्तरम् आनयति । अथैतद् अग्निहोत्रम् अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य पूर्वया द्वारा प्रपाद्य जघनेन गार्हपत्यम् उपसाद्य तस्मिन्न् अग्निहोत्रविधिं चेष्टित्वा समिधम् उपयत्य प्राङ् हरति
2.18.65.m: Having put [the milk] on the fire, he pours water into it. Then, having brought this agnihotra [milk] around in front of the āhavanīya fire, having brought it in through the eastern door, having set it down behind the gārhapatya fire, having performed the procedure of the agnihotra over it, having taken up the kindling stick, he carries it east.
He sets it down on a grass cushion behind the āhavanīya fire.
Here he puts this kindling stick into the middle of the āhavanīya fire silently.

2.18.65.s: tasyām ādīptāyāṃ pratimukhaṃ dvir juhoty uc ca mārṣṭy ava ca mārṣṭy ubhayam avāpnoti | iti brāhmaṇam |
2.18.65.d: तस्याम् आदीप्तायां प्रतिमुखं द्विर् जुहोत्य् उच् च मार्ष्ट्य् अव च मार्ष्ट्य् उभयम् अवाप्नोति । इति ब्राह्मणम् ।
2.18.65.m: "When it is ablaze, he offers twice facing it; he wipes up and he wipes down; he obtains both"—so says the brāhmaṇa passage.

2.18.65.s: dvir aṅgulyā prāśyodaṅ paryāvṛtya prācīnadaṇḍayā srucā bhakṣayati
2.18.65.d: द्विर् अङ्गुल्या प्राश्योदङ् पर्यावृत्य प्राचीनदण्डया स्रुचा भक्षयति
2.18.65.m: Having consumed twice with the finger, having turned around facing north, he consumes with the ladle pointing east.
Having washed the ladle, having heated it, having filled it with water, he points it to the north.
"He pleases the Seven Seers themselves"—so says the brāhmaṇa passage.

2.18.65.s: hutvopasaminddhe brahmavarcasasya samiddhyai | apo ninayaty avabhṛthasyaiva rūpam akar iti brāhmaṇam ||
2.18.65.d: हुत्वोपसमिन्द्धे ब्रह्मवर्चसस्य समिद्ध्यै । अपो निनयत्य् अवभृथस्यैव रूपम् अकर् इति ब्राह्मणम् ॥
2.18.65.m: "Having offered, he kindles [the fire] for the kindling of spiritual lustre; he pours out the water: he has made the very form of the final bath"—so says the brāhmaṇa passage.

2.19.66.s: atha parikarmiṇaṃ barhir lāvaṃ prahiṇoti | āhṛtaṃ vā yajuṣā karoti |
2.19.66.d: अथ परिकर्मिणं बर्हिर् लावं प्रहिणोति । आहृतं वा यजुषा करोति ।
2.19.66.m: Then he sends an attendant to cut sacrificial grass, or he prepares with a yajus formula what has been brought.

2.19.66.s: atha pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyāgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapsyan daśahotāraṃ vyācakṣīta
2.19.66.d: अथ पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयाग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वप्स्यन् दशहोतारं व्याचक्षीत
2.19.66.m: Then, having strewn along the spinal line, having brought forward the waters, intending to mete out [the oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni, he should recite the Daśahotṛ formula.
Intending to recite the kindling verses, he should recite the Daśahotṛ formula.

2.19.66.s: śrapayitvāsādayati tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau |
2.19.66.d: श्रपयित्वासादयति तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ ।
2.19.66.m: Having cooked [the cake], he sets it down. Its kindling verses are fifteen, the preliminary offerings five, the two butter portions are vṛtra-slaying.

2.19.66.s: atha haviṣas | agnir mūrdhā bhuvas | iti
2.19.66.d: अथ हविषस् । अग्निर् मूर्धा भुवस् । इति
2.19.66.m: Then for the oblation: "Agni is head…", "Become…"

2.19.66.s: triṣṭubhau saṃyājye anvāhāryam āsādyāgnyādheyadakṣiṇā dadāti | ā dvādaśabhyo dadāti
2.19.66.d: त्रिष्टुभौ संयाज्ये अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्याग्न्याधेयदक्षिणा ददाति । आ द्वादशभ्यो ददाति
2.19.66.m: The two offering verses are in triṣṭubh metre. Having set down the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives the sacrificial gifts for the fire-establishment; he gives up to twelve [cows].

2.19.66.s: kāmaṃ bhūyasīr dadāti saṃtiṣṭhata eṣeṣṭiḥ sapūrṇapātraviṣṇukramā
2.19.66.d: कामं भूयसीर् ददाति संतिष्ठत एषेष्टिः सपूर्णपात्रविष्णुक्रमा
2.19.66.m: At will he gives more. This offering is concluded along with the full vessel [gift] and the Viṣṇu strides.

2.19.66.s: visṛjate vratam atha tadānīm eva pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyaindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapaty ādityaṃ carum |
2.19.66.d: विसृजते व्रतम् अथ तदानीम् एव पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयैन्द्राग्नम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपत्य् आदित्यं चरुम् ।
2.19.66.m: He releases the vow. Then, right at that time, having strewn along the spinal line, having brought forward the waters, he metes out [the oblation] on eleven potsherds for Indra-Agni, and a caru for Aditi.
When it is cooked, or even nearer [completion], he pours ghee [into it]. Having cooked [it], he sets it down.

2.19.66.s: tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau |
2.19.66.d: तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ ।
2.19.66.m: Its kindling verses are fifteen, the preliminary offerings five, the two butter portions are vṛtra-slaying.

2.19.66.s: atha haviṣos | indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ śnathad vṛtram ity aindrāgnasya |
2.19.66.d: अथ हविषोस् । इन्द्राग्नी रोचना दिवः श्नथद् वृत्रम् इत्य् ऐन्द्राग्नस्य ।
2.19.66.m: Then for the two oblations: "Indra and Agni, the luminaries of heaven…", "Smote Vṛtra…" for the offering to Indra-Agni;

2.19.66.s: aditir na uruṣyatu mahīm ū ṣu mātaram ity ādityasya
2.19.66.d: अदितिर् न उरुष्यतु महीम् ऊ षु मातरम् इत्य् आदित्यस्य
2.19.66.m: "May Aditi protect us…", "The great mother…" for the offering to Aditi.

2.19.66.s: triṣṭubhau saṃyājye anvāhāryam āsādyāthaitaṃ caruṃ vyuddhṛtya catvāra ārṣeyāḥ prāśnanti
2.19.66.d: त्रिष्टुभौ संयाज्ये अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्याथैतं चरुं व्युद्धृत्य चत्वार आर्षेयाः प्राश्नन्ति
2.19.66.m: The two offering verses are in triṣṭubh metre. Having set down the anvāhārya cooked rice, then having taken out this caru, four [priests] of ṛṣi descent consume it.

2.19.66.s: diśām eva jyotiṣi juhoti | iti brāhmaṇam |
2.19.66.d: दिशाम् एव ज्योतिषि जुहोति । इति ब्राह्मणम् ।
2.19.66.m: "He offers into the very light of the quarters"—so says the brāhmaṇa passage.
This offering is concluded along with the full vessel [gift] and the Viṣṇu strides. He releases the vow.

2.20.66.s: atraitad dvādaśāhaṃ vrataṃ carati tasyaitad vratam | nānṛtaṃ vadati
2.20.66.d: अत्रैतद् द्वादशाहं व्रतं चरति तस्यैतद् व्रतम् । नानृतं वदति
2.20.66.m: Here he observes a twelve-day vow. This is his vow: he does not speak falsehood;

2.20.66.s: na mām̐sam aśnāti na striyam upaiti nāsya palpūlanena vāsaḥ palpūlayanti |
2.20.66.d: न माँसम् अश्नाति न स्त्रियम् उपैति नास्य पल्पूलनेन वासः पल्पूलयन्ति ।
2.20.66.m: he does not eat meat; he does not approach a woman; they do not wash his garment with alkaline water;
he does not drink from an earthen vessel; he does not eat the remnants of a śūdra; he washes his feet himself;

2.20.67.s: na lavaṇam aśnāti na kauśīdhānyam anyatra tilebhyaḥ prāṅ uccāraḥ svayam̐ samidha āharamāṇo 'gnīnām ante saṃviśati |
2.20.67.d: न लवणम् अश्नाति न कौशीधान्यम् अन्यत्र तिलेभ्यः प्राङ् उच्चारः स्वयँ समिध आहरमाणो ऽग्नीनाम् अन्ते संविशति ।
2.20.67.m: he does not eat salt; [he does not eat] pod-grain except sesame seeds; he voids excrement facing east; fetching kindling sticks himself, he sleeps near the fires.
These fires of his remain uninterruptedly burning for twelve days.
No brahmin stays fasting in his house.

2.20.67.s: agnihotroccheṣaṇavrato vā yajamāno bhavati bhaktam u patnyā āharanti |
2.20.67.d: अग्निहोत्रोच्छेषणव्रतो वा यजमानो भवति भक्तम् उ पत्न्या आहरन्ति ।
2.20.67.m: Or the sacrificer observes the vow of eating the agnihotra remnants; and they fetch cooked food for his wife.

2.20.67.s: atha dvādaśasu vyuṣṭāsu pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyāgnaye pavamānāya puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati
2.20.67.d: अथ द्वादशसु व्युष्टासु पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयाग्नये पवमानाय पुरोडाशम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपति
2.20.67.m: Then, when twelve [dawns] have shone forth, having strewn along the spinal line, having brought forward the waters, he metes out a cake on eight potsherds for Agni Pavamāna.

2.20.67.s: tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau | atha haviṣas | agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase | agne pavasva | iti
2.20.67.d: तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ । अथ हविषस् । अग्न आयूँषि पवसे । अग्ने पवस्व । इति
2.20.67.m: Its kindling verses are fifteen, the preliminary offerings five, the two butter portions are vṛtra-slaying. Then for the oblation: "O Agni, you purify lifespans…", "O Agni, purify yourself…"

2.20.67.s: anvāhāryam āsādya trim̐śanmānam̐ hiraṇyaṃ dadāti saṃtiṣṭhata eṣeṣṭiḥ sapūrṇapātraviṣṇukramā
2.20.67.d: अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्य त्रिँशन्मानँ हिरण्यं ददाति संतिष्ठत एषेष्टिः सपूर्णपात्रविष्णुक्रमा
2.20.67.m: Having set down the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives a piece of gold thirty units in weight. This offering is concluded along with the full vessel [gift] and the Viṣṇu strides.

2.20.67.s: visṛjate vratam atha tadānīm eva pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyāgnaye pāvakāya puroḍāśam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapaty agnaye śucaye
2.20.67.d: विसृजते व्रतम् अथ तदानीम् एव पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयाग्नये पावकाय पुरोडाशम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपत्य् अग्नये शुचये
2.20.67.m: He releases the vow. Then, right at that time, having strewn along the spinal line, having brought forward the waters, he metes out a cake on eight potsherds for Agni Pāvaka, [and one] for Agni Śuci.

2.20.67.s: śrapayitvāsādayati tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāvājyabhāgau |
2.20.67.d: श्रपयित्वासादयति तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नावाज्यभागौ ।
2.20.67.m: Having cooked [them], he sets them down. Its kindling verses are fifteen, the preliminary offerings five, the two butter portions are vṛtra-slaying.

2.20.67.s: atha haviṣos | agne pāvaka sa naḥ pāvaka | agniḥ śucivratatamas | ud agne śucayas tava | iti
2.20.67.d: अथ हविषोस् । अग्ने पावक स नः पावक । अग्निः शुचिव्रततमस् । उद् अग्ने शुचयस् तव । इति
2.20.67.m: Then for the two oblations: "O Agni Pāvaka…", "He to us, O Pāvaka…"; "Agni of purest vows…", "Upward, O Agni, your pure…"

2.20.67.s: triṣṭubhau saṃyājye anvāhāryam āsādya trim̐śanmānacatvārim̐śanmāne hiraṇye dadāti
2.20.67.d: त्रिष्टुभौ संयाज्ये अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्य त्रिँशन्मानचत्वारिँशन्माने हिरण्ये ददाति
2.20.67.m: The two offering verses are in triṣṭubh metre. Having set down the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives gold pieces of thirty and forty units in weight.
This offering is concluded along with the full vessel [gift] and the Viṣṇu strides.

2.21.67.s: athāto 'nvārambhasyaiva mīmām̐sā | anvārambhaṃ paurṇamāsyāḥ samānopavasathaṃ karoti |
2.21.67.d: अथातो ऽन्वारम्भस्यैव मीमाँसा । अन्वारम्भं पौर्णमास्याः समानोपवसथं करोति ।
2.21.67.m: Now follows the discussion of the initial offering. He performs the initial offering on the same fast-day as the full moon ritual.

2.21.67.s: atha prātarhute 'gnihotre purāpāṃ praṇayanād gārhapatya ājyaṃ vilāpyotpūya sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā caturhotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye juhoty anvārabdhe yajamāne svāhā | iti |
2.21.67.d: अथ प्रातर्हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे पुरापां प्रणयनाद् गार्हपत्य आज्यं विलाप्योत्पूय स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा चतुर्होतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये जुहोत्य् अन्वारब्धे यजमाने स्वाहा । इति ।
2.21.67.m: Then, when the morning agnihotra has been offered, prior to the bringing forward of the waters, having melted ghee over the gārhapatya fire and purified it, having taken four ladlings in the ladle, having recited mentally the Caturhotṛ formula, he offers into the āhavanīya fire while the sacrificer holds onto him, with: "Svāhā!"

2.21.68.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sārasvatau homau juhoti
2.21.68.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा सारस्वतौ होमौ जुहोति
2.21.68.m: Having taken another four ladlings, he offers the two Sārasvata libations.

2.21.68.s: pūrṇā paścāt | ity anudrutya | agnīṣomau | iti juhoti | aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā niveśanī saṃgamanī vasūnām ity anudrutya yat te devā adadhur bhāgadheyam iti juhoti |
2.21.68.d: पूर्णा पश्चात् । इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य । अग्नीषोमौ । इति जुहोति । अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा निवेशनी संगमनी वसूनाम् इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य यत् ते देवा अदधुर् भागधेयम् इति जुहोति ।
2.21.68.m: Having recited in one breath, "Full from behind," he offers with, "O Agni and Soma!" / Having taken another four ladlings and recited in one breath, "Bestower of dwelling, gatherer of riches," he offers with, "Which share the gods assigned to you."

2.21.68.s: atha pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyāgnāvaiśṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati sarasvatyai carum̐ sarasvate dvādaśakapālam iti
2.21.68.d: अथ पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयाग्नावैश्णवम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपति सरस्वत्यै चरुँ सरस्वते द्वादशकपालम् इति
2.21.68.m: Then, having spread [grass along] the central line and brought forward the waters, he sets aside [an oblation] on eleven potsherds for Agni and Viṣṇu, a pap for Sarasvatī, [and an oblation] on twelve potsherds for Sarasvant.

2.21.68.s: śrapayitvāsādayati tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau |
2.21.68.d: श्रपयित्वासादयति तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ ।
2.21.68.m: Having cooked [them], he places [them] down. / It has fifteen kindling verses, five fore-offerings, and the two portions of melted butter are [accompanied by] the 'Vṛtra-killing' [verses].

2.21.68.s: atha haviṣām agnāviṣṇū agnāviṣṇū pra ṇo devī | ā no divaḥ pīpivām̐sam̐ sarasvata stanam | ye te sarasva ūrmayas | iti
2.21.68.d: अथ हविषाम् अग्नाविष्णू अग्नाविष्णू प्र णो देवी । आ नो दिवः पीपिवाँसँ सरस्वत स्तनम् । ये ते सरस्व ऊर्मयस् । इति
2.21.68.m: Then for the oblations [the verses are]: "O Agni and Viṣṇu," "O Agni and Viṣṇu," "May the goddess [Sarasvatī] to us," "To us from heaven," "The swelling breast of Sarasvant," [and] "Those waves of yours, O Sarasvant."

2.21.68.s: triṣṭubhau saṃyājye anvāhāryam āsādya mithunau gāvau dadāti
2.21.68.d: त्रिष्टुभौ संयाज्ये अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्य मिथुनौ गावौ ददाति
2.21.68.m: The two offering-formulas are in triṣṭubh metre. / Having placed the anvāhārya cooked rice down, he gives a pair of cattle.
This sacrifice concludes with the full-cup [ritual] and the Viṣṇu-strides.
He releases his vow. / Then he sacrifices with the full moon and Vaimṛdha [offerings].
The establishment of the fires is concluded; the establishment of the fires is concluded.

3.1.69.s: agnīn punarādhāsyamāno bhavati tad āhus | kṛtayajuḥ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro bhavati na saṃbhṛtyāḥ saṃbhārā na yajuḥ kartavyam iti |
3.1.69.d: अग्नीन् पुनराधास्यमानो भवति तद् आहुस् । कृतयजुः संभृतसंभारो भवति न संभृत्याः संभारा न यजुः कर्तव्यम् इति ।
3.1.69.m: He is about to re-establish the fires. / About that they say: "His formulas have [already] been performed, his materials collected; materials are not to be collected, nor is a formula to be recited."

3.1.69.s: atho khalu saṃbhṛtyā eva saṃbhārāḥ kartavyaṃ yajuḥ punarādheyasya samṛddhyai | iti
3.1.69.d: अथो खलु संभृत्या एव संभाराः कर्तव्यं यजुः पुनराधेयस्य समृद्ध्यै । इति
3.1.69.m: "On the contrary, materials are indeed to be collected, and a formula recited, for the success of the re-establishment."

3.1.69.s: sa upakalpayate punarniṣkṛtam̐ rathaṃ punarutsyūtaṃ vāsaḥ punarutsṛṣṭam anaḍvāhaṃ darbhakulāyaṃ tisro darbhamayīr visūrmikāḥ
3.1.69.d: स उपकल्पयते पुनर्निष्कृतँ रथं पुनरुत्स्यूतं वासः पुनरुत्सृष्टम् अनड्वाहं दर्भकुलायं तिस्रो दर्भमयीर् विसूर्मिकाः
3.1.69.m: He procures a repaired chariot, a re-stitched garment, a re-released ox, a nest of darbha grass, [and] three rolls made of darbha grass.

3.1.69.s: prajñātā āgnyādheyikāḥ saṃbhārāḥ sā yāṣāḍhyāḥ paurṇamāsyāḥ purastād amāvāsyā bhavati sā sakṛt saṃvatsarasya punarvasubhyām̐ saṃpadyate tasyām ādadhīta | iti
3.1.69.d: प्रज्ञाता आग्न्याधेयिकाः संभाराः सा याषाढ्याः पौर्णमास्याः पुरस्ताद् अमावास्या भवति सा सकृत् संवत्सरस्य पुनर्वसुभ्याँ संपद्यते तस्याम् आदधीत । इति
3.1.69.m: The materials for the establishment of the sacred fires are known. / "The new moon which occurs before the full moon of Āṣāḍhī, that [new moon] coincides once a year with the Punarvasus; on that one should establish [the fires]."

3.1.69.s: tasyā upavasathe 'raṇyor agnīn samārohyodavasāya mathitvāgnīn vihṛtyāgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālam agnim udvāsayiṣyan | iti
3.1.69.d: तस्या उपवसथे ऽरण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्योदवसाय मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्याग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपति वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालम् अग्निम् उद्वासयिष्यन् । इति
3.1.69.m: On its fast-day, having caused the fires to mount into the two churning-sticks, having departed, churned [fire], and spread out the fires, he sets aside [an oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni [and an oblation] on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara, intending to remove the fire.

3.1.69.s: atha tadānīm evādbhir agnīn samukṣya brahmaudanam̐ śrapayitvopavasati |
3.1.69.d: अथ तदानीम् एवाद्भिर् अग्नीन् समुक्ष्य ब्रह्मौदनँ श्रपयित्वोपवसति ।
3.1.69.m: Then right at that time, having sprinkled the fires with water and cooked the brahmins' boiled rice, he keeps the fast.

3.1.69.s: atha prātarāgnyādheyikaṃ karma tāyate | etāvad eva nānā
3.1.69.d: अथ प्रातराग्न्याधेयिकं कर्म तायते । एतावद् एव नाना
3.1.69.m: Then in the morning the rite of the establishment of the sacred fires is performed. / Only this much is different:

3.1.69.s: yad amutra muñjakulāyaṃ tad iha darbhakulāyam | yo 'mutredhmaḥ praṇayanīyaḥ sa iha darbhamayīr visūrmikā
3.1.69.d: यद् अमुत्र मुञ्जकुलायं तद् इह दर्भकुलायम् । यो ऽमुत्रेध्मः प्रणयनीयः स इह दर्भमयीर् विसूर्मिका
3.1.69.m: What was there a nest of muñja grass, is here a nest of darbha grass. / What was there the kindling wood to be carried forward, is here the three rolls made of darbha grass.

3.1.69.s: darbhair gārhapatyam ādadhāti darbhair anvāhāryapacanaṃ darbhair āhavanīyam |
3.1.69.d: दर्भैर् गार्हपत्यम् आदधाति दर्भैर् अन्वाहार्यपचनं दर्भैर् आहवनीयम् ।
3.1.69.m: He establishes the gārhapatya with darbha grass, the anvāhāryapacana with darbha grass, [and] the āhavanīya with darbha grass.
He establishes the gārhapatya with darbha grass.
During the establishment, he follows up with the Sarparājñī verses.

3.2.69.s: bhūmir bhūmnā dyaur variṇā | iti catasro gārhapatye tisra āhavanīye
3.2.69.d: भूमिर् भूम्ना द्यौर् वरिणा । इति चतस्रो गार्हपत्ये तिस्र आहवनीये
3.2.69.m: "The earth in extent, the heaven in width," with these [formulas he puts on] four [pieces of fuel] on the gārhapatya, [and] three on the āhavanīya.

3.2.70.s: samānaṃ karmā rathacakrāt | etāvad eva nānā yad amutra tūṣṇīm agnihotraṃ tad iha sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvās | iti juhoti
3.2.70.d: समानं कर्मा रथचक्रात् । एतावद् एव नाना यद् अमुत्र तूष्णीम् अग्निहोत्रं तद् इह सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वास् । इति जुहोति
3.2.70.m: The rite is the same up to the chariot-wheel. / Only this much is different: / what was there the silent agnihotra, here he offers with, "Seven are your kindling sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues."

3.2.70.d: यो ऽमुत्राग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः स इहाग्नेयः पञ्चकपालस्
3.2.70.m: What was there an [oblation] on eight potsherds for Agni, is here on five potsherds for Agni.

3.2.70.s: tasya prayājeṣu catasro vibhaktīr dadhāti | agna āyāhi vītaye samidho agna ājyasya viyantu | agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe tanūnapād agna ājyasya vetu | agnināgniḥ samidhyate | iḍo agna ājyasya viyantu | agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat | barhir agna ājyasya vetu | iti
3.2.70.d: तस्य प्रयाजेषु चतस्रो विभक्तीर् दधाति । अग्न आयाहि वीतये समिधो अग्न आज्यस्य वियन्तु । अग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे तनूनपाद् अग्न आज्यस्य वेतु । अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते । इडो अग्न आज्यस्य वियन्तु । अग्निर् वृत्राणि जङ्घनत् । बर्हिर् अग्न आज्यस्य वेतु । इति
3.2.70.m: At its fore-offerings, he applies the four modified verses: "O Agni, come for the feast," "May the kindling sticks, O Agni, partake of the melted butter"; "Agni we choose as messenger," "May Tanūnapāt, O Agni, partake of the melted butter"; "Fire is kindled by fire," "May the refreshments, O Agni, partake of the melted butter"; "Agni shall slay the Vṛtras," "May the barhis, O Agni, partake of the melted butter."
The last fore-offering is completed by itself.

3.2.70.s: athāta ājyabhāgayor eva mīmām̐sā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau syātām ity eke
3.2.70.d: अथात आज्यभागयोर् एव मीमाँसा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ स्याताम् इत्य् एके
3.2.70.m: Now then is the discussion regarding the two portions of melted butter. / Some say that the two portions of melted butter should be [accompanied by] the 'Vṛtra-killing' [verses].
Some say they should be [accompanied by] the 'prosperity-bearing' [verses].

3.2.70.s: agnim̐ stomena bodhaya tvaṃ naḥ soma | ity etau syātām ity eke | agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase | agne pavasva | ity etau syātām ity eke
3.2.70.d: अग्निँ स्तोमेन बोधय त्वं नः सोम । इत्य् एतौ स्याताम् इत्य् एके । अग्न आयूँषि पवसे । अग्ने पवस्व । इत्य् एतौ स्याताम् इत्य् एके
3.2.70.m: Some say they should be these two: "Awaken Agni with praise," "You to us, O Soma." / Some say they should be these two: "O Agni, you purify our life-spans," "O Agni, purify."
That which belongs to Pavamāna is of the nature of Soma.

3.2.70.s: paṅktyau haviṣas | agne tam adya | adhā hy agne | iti | atha punar ūrjā saha rayyā | ity abhitaḥ puroḍāśam āhutī juhoti |
3.2.70.d: पङ्क्त्यौ हविषस् । अग्ने तम् अद्य । अधा ह्य् अग्ने । इति । अथ पुनर् ऊर्जा सह रय्या । इत्य् अभितः पुरोडाशम् आहुती जुहोति ।
3.2.70.m: The two [verses] for the oblation are in paṅkti metre: "Agni, that today," "For thus, O Agni." / Then on both sides of the cake he offers two oblations with, "With strength again," [and] "Together with wealth."

3.2.70.s: agniṃ prati sviṣṭakṛtaṃ nirāha | ābhiṣ ṭe adya ebhir no arkais | iti saṃyājye
3.2.70.d: अग्निं प्रति स्विष्टकृतं निराह । आभिष् टे अद्य एभिर् नो अर्कैस् । इति संयाज्ये
3.2.70.m: For Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, he speaks out [the verses]; the two offering-formulas are: "With these today for you," [and] "With these songs for us."

3.3.70.s: punarādheyadakṣiṇā dadāti punarniṣkṛtam̐ rathaṃ punarutsyūtaṃ vāsaḥ punarutsṛṣṭam anaḍvāham |
3.3.70.d: पुनराधेयदक्षिणा ददाति पुनर्निष्कृतँ रथं पुनरुत्स्यूतं वासः पुनरुत्सृष्टम् अनड्वाहम् ।
3.3.70.m: he gives the priestly fee for the re-establishment: a repaired chariot, a re-stitched garment, [and] a re-released ox.

3.3.70.s: tasyānūyājeṣu vibhaktī dadhāti | agnā yo martyo duvas | dhiyaṃ jujoṣa dhītibhiḥ | bhasan nu ṣa pra pūrvyas | iṣaṃ vurītāvase | devaṃ barhir vasuvane vasudheyasya vetu | agne stomaṃ manāmahe sidhram adya divispṛśaḥ | devasya draviṇasyavas | devo narāśam̐so vasuvane vasudheyasya vetu | iti
3.3.70.d: तस्यानूयाजेषु विभक्ती दधाति । अग्ना यो मर्त्यो दुवस् । धियं जुजोष धीतिभिः । भसन् नु ष प्र पूर्व्यस् । इषं वुरीतावसे । देवं बर्हिर् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु । अग्ने स्तोमं मनामहे सिध्रम् अद्य दिविस्पृशः । देवस्य द्रविणस्यवस् । देवो नराशँसो वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु । इति
3.3.70.m: At its after-offerings, he applies the modified verses: / "O Agni, which mortal serves / [and] takes delight in devotion with pious thoughts, / may he, foremost, consuming now / choose vigor for help"; / "May the divine barhis partake of the wealth for the winning of wealth"; / "Agni's praise we ponder, / effective today reaching to heaven, / seeking the wealth of the god"; / "May divine Narāśaṃsa partake of the wealth for the winning of wealth."

3.3.71.m: The last after-offering is completed by itself.
This sacrifice concludes with the full-cup [ritual] and the Viṣṇu-strides. / He releases his vow.

3.3.71.s: atha tadānīm eva pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ prāṇīyāgnivāruṇam ekādaśakapālam anunirvapati
3.3.71.d: अथ तदानीम् एव पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्राणीयाग्निवारुणम् एकादशकपालम् अनुनिर्वपति
3.3.71.m: Then right at that time, having spread [grass along] the central line and brought forward the waters, he sets aside following [this] an oblation on eleven potsherds for Agni and Varuṇa.

3.3.71.s: śrapayitvāsādayati tasyāḥ pañcadaśa sāmidhenyaḥ pañca prayājā vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau |
3.3.71.d: श्रपयित्वासादयति तस्याः पञ्चदश सामिधेन्यः पञ्च प्रयाजा वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ ।
3.3.71.m: Having cooked [it], he places [it] down. / It has fifteen kindling verses, five fore-offerings, and the two portions of melted butter are [accompanied by] the 'Vṛtra-killing' [verses].

3.3.71.s: atha haviṣas tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne | iti
3.3.71.d: अथ हविषस् त्वं नो अग्ने स त्वं नो अग्ने । इति
3.3.71.m: Then for the oblation [the verses are]: "You to us, O Agni," [and] "So you to us, O Agni."
The two offering-formulas are in triṣṭubh metre. / Having placed the anvāhārya cooked rice down, he gives an ox.
This sacrifice concludes with the full-cup [ritual] and the Viṣṇu-strides.

3.3.71.s: visṛjate vratam | saṃtiṣṭhate punarādheyam iti nv ṛddhipunarādheyam
3.3.71.d: विसृजते व्रतम् । संतिष्ठते पुनराधेयम् इति न्व् ऋद्धिपुनराधेयम्
3.3.71.m: He releases his vow. / The re-establishment [of the fires] is concluded. / Thus indeed is the re-establishment for prosperity.

3.3.71.s: atha vai bhavati yaḥ parācīnaṃ punarādheyād agnim ādadhīta sa etān homāñ juhuyāt | iti
3.3.71.d: अथ वै भवति यः पराचीनं पुनराधेयाद् अग्निम् आदधीत स एतान् होमाञ् जुहुयात् । इति
3.3.71.m: Now indeed it is said: / "He who should establish the fire beyond a re-establishment, let him offer these oblations."

3.3.71.s: tṛtīyam ādhāna āgneyasya pañcakapālasya purastāt sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sruvāhutīr upajuhoti lekaḥ salekaḥ sulekas te na ādityā ājyaṃ juṣāṇā viyantu svāhā | ketaḥ saketaḥ suketas te na ādityā ājyaṃ juṣāṇā viyantu svāhā | vivasvām̐ aditir devajūtis te na ādityā ājyaṃ juṣāṇā viyantu svāhā | iti
3.3.71.d: तृतीयम् आधान आग्नेयस्य पञ्चकपालस्य पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतः स्रुवाहुतीर् उपजुहोति लेकः सलेकः सुलेकस् ते न आदित्या आज्यं जुषाणा वियन्तु स्वाहा । केतः सकेतः सुकेतस् ते न आदित्या आज्यं जुषाणा वियन्तु स्वाहा । विवस्वाँ अदितिर् देवजूतिस् ते न आदित्या आज्यं जुषाणा वियन्तु स्वाहा । इति
3.3.71.m: At a third establishment, before [the oblation to] Sviṣṭakṛt of the [offering] on five potsherds for Agni, he offers additional ladle libations: "Leka, Saleka, Suleka, may these Ādityas, enjoying the melted butter, partake of it, svāhā!"; "Keta, Saketa, Suketa, may these Ādityas, enjoying the melted butter, partake of it, svāhā!"; "Vivasvant, Aditi, the impulse of the gods, may these Ādityas, enjoying the melted butter, partake of it, svāhā!"

3.3.71.s: saṃtiṣṭhate tṛtīyam ādhānam athāpahṛtāgner naṣṭāraṇīkasya ca brahmaudanenaiva pratipadyate
3.3.71.d: संतिष्ठते तृतीयम् आधानम् अथापहृताग्नेर् नष्टारणीकस्य च ब्रह्मौदनेनैव प्रतिपद्यते
3.3.71.m: The third establishment is concluded. / Now, in the case of one whose fire has been carried away or whose churning-sticks have been lost, he undertakes [the rite] with the brahmins' boiled rice alone.

3.4.72.s: purastād ity asyāstamayād gārhapatyam upasamādhāyānvāhāryapacanam āhṛtya jvalantam āhavanīyam uddharati sāyamāhutaye
3.4.72.d: पुरस्ताद् इत्य् अस्यास्तमयाद् गार्हपत्यम् उपसमाधायान्वाहार्यपचनम् आहृत्य ज्वलन्तम् आहवनीयम् उद्धरति सायमाहुतये
3.4.72.m: Before the sunset of this [sun], having added fuel to the gārhapatya fire and brought [embers for] the anvāhāryapacana, he lifts out the flaming āhavanīya fire for the evening offering.

3.4.72.s: purastād ity asyodayād gārhapatyam upasamādhāyānvāhāryapacanam āhṛtya jvalantam āhavanīyam uddharati prātarāhutaye
3.4.72.d: पुरस्ताद् इत्य् अस्योदयाद् गार्हपत्यम् उपसमाधायान्वाहार्यपचनम् आहृत्य ज्वलन्तम् आहवनीयम् उद्धरति प्रातराहुतये
3.4.72.m: Before the sunrise of this [sun], having added fuel to the gārhapatya fire and brought [embers for] the anvāhāryapacana, he lifts out the flaming āhavanīya fire for the morning offering.

3.4.72.s: vācā tvā hotrā prāṇenodgātrā cakṣuṣādhvaryuṇā manasā brahmaṇā śrotreṇāgnīdhaitais tvā pañcabhir daivyair ṛtvigbhir uddharāmi bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar uddhriyamāṇa uddhara pāpmano mā yad avidvān yac ca vidvām̐ś cakāra | ahnā yad enaḥ kṛtam asti pāpam | sarvasmān moddhṛto muñca tasmāt | iti sāyam |
3.4.72.d: वाचा त्वा होत्रा प्राणेनोद्गात्रा चक्षुषाध्वर्युणा मनसा ब्रह्मणा श्रोत्रेणाग्नीधैतैस् त्वा पञ्चभिर् दैव्यैर् ऋत्विग्भिर् उद्धरामि भूर् भुवः सुवर् उद्ध्रियमाण उद्धर पाप्मनो मा यद् अविद्वान् यच् च विद्वाँश् चकार । अह्ना यद् एनः कृतम् अस्ति पापम् । सर्वस्मान् मोद्धृतो मुञ्च तस्मात् । इति सायम् ।
3.4.72.m: "With speech as hotṛ priest, with breath as udgātṛ priest, with sight as adhvaryu priest, with mind as brahman priest, with hearing as agnīdh priest—with these five divine officiating priests I take you up. Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar! Being taken up, take me up from evil: whatever [evil] I have done unknowing or knowing, / whatever sinful offense has been committed by day, / from all that, being taken up, release me!"—thus in the evening.

3.4.72.s: rātriyā yad enaḥ kṛtam asti pāpam | sarvasmān moddhṛto muñca tasmāt | iti prātar
3.4.72.d: रात्रिया यद् एनः कृतम् अस्ति पापम् । सर्वस्मान् मोद्धृतो मुञ्च तस्मात् । इति प्रातर्
3.4.72.m: "Whatever sinful offense has been committed by night, / from all that, being taken up, release me!"—thus in the morning.

3.4.72.s: agniṃ nidadhāti | amṛtāhutim amṛtāyāṃ juhomi | agniṃ pṛthivyām amṛtasya jityai | tayānantaṃ kāmam ito jayema prajāpatir yaṃ prathamo jigāya | agnim agnau vaiśvānare 'mṛtaṃ juhomi svāhā | iti sāyam |
3.4.72.d: अग्निं निदधाति । अमृताहुतिम् अमृतायां जुहोमि । अग्निं पृथिव्याम् अमृतस्य जित्यै । तयानन्तं कामम् इतो जयेम प्रजापतिर् यं प्रथमो जिगाय । अग्निम् अग्नौ वैश्वानरे ऽमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहा । इति सायम् ।
3.4.72.m: He sets down the fire: "I offer the immortal oblation into the immortal [fire], / Agni into the earth, for the winning of immortality. / Through it may we win unlimited desire from here, / which Prajāpati first won. / Agni into Agni Vaiśvānara, immortal, I offer, svāhā!"—thus in the evening.

3.4.72.s: sūryam agnau vaiśvānare 'mṛtaṃ juhomi svāhā | iti prātaḥ
3.4.72.d: सूर्यम् अग्नौ वैश्वानरे ऽमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहा । इति प्रातः
3.4.72.m: "Sūrya into Agni Vaiśvānara, immortal, I offer, svāhā!"—thus in the morning.
Every evening and morning this wife sits nearby.

3.4.72.s: sāyam̐sāyam ity eke | athaitāny agnihotrapātrāṇi prakṣālitāny uttareṇa gārhapatyam upasādayati kūrce vā sūnāyāṃ vā sthālīṃ sasruvām̐ srucam abhidyotanam̐ samidham iti |
3.4.72.d: सायँसायम् इत्य् एके । अथैतान्य् अग्निहोत्रपात्राणि प्रक्षालितान्य् उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यम् उपसादयति कूर्चे वा सूनायां वा स्थालीं सस्रुवाँ स्रुचम् अभिद्योतनँ समिधम् इति ।
3.4.72.m: "Every evening [only]," say some. Then he places these rinsed agnihotra vessels north of the gārhapatya fire on a grass bundle or in a wicker basket: the pot, the ladle with the spoon, the illuminator, and the kindling stick.

3.4.72.s: athaitām agnihotrīṃ dakṣiṇata udīcīm̐ sthāpayitvā brāhmaṇo dogdhi
3.4.72.d: अथैताम् अग्निहोत्रीं दक्षिणत उदीचीँ स्थापयित्वा ब्राह्मणो दोग्धि
3.4.72.m: Then, having stationed this agnihotra cow south facing north, a brāhmaṇa milks [her].

3.4.73.s: pūrvau duhyāj jyeṣṭhasya jyaiṣṭhineyasya yo vā gataśrīḥ syāt |
3.4.73.d: पूर्वौ दुह्याज् ज्येष्ठस्य ज्यैष्ठिनेयस्य यो वा गतश्रीः स्यात् ।
3.4.73.m: "He should milk the two front [teats] for an eldest son, for the son of a senior wife, or for one who would be prosperous.

3.4.73.s: aparau duhyāt kaniṣṭhasya kāniṣṭhineyasya yo vā bubhūṣet |
3.4.73.d: अपरौ दुह्यात् कनिष्ठस्य कानिष्ठिनेयस्य यो वा बुभूषेत् ।
3.4.73.m: He should milk the two rear [teats] for a youngest son, for the son of a junior wife, or for one who wishes to thrive.

3.4.73.s: na saṃmṛśet | dvayor duhyāt paśukāmasya | iti |
3.4.73.d: न संमृशेत् । द्वयोर् दुह्यात् पशुकामस्य । इति ।
3.4.73.m: He should not touch them [both]. He should milk two for one desiring cattle"—thus [says the Brāhmaṇa].

3.4.73.s: adhiśrityottaram ānayati | athaitad agnihotram agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya pūrvayā dvārā prapādya jaghanena gārhapatyam upasādyātha pariṣiñcati ||
3.4.73.d: अधिश्रित्योत्तरम् आनयति । अथैतद् अग्निहोत्रम् अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य पूर्वया द्वारा प्रपाद्य जघनेन गार्हपत्यम् उपसाद्याथ परिषिञ्चति ॥
3.4.73.m: Having placed [the pot] on the fire, he brings in water. Then, having carried this agnihotra milk around in front of the āhavanīya fire, having brought it in through the eastern door, and having set it down behind the gārhapatya fire, he then sprinkles around.

3.5.73.s: ṛtaṃ tvā satyena pariṣiñcāmi | iti sāyaṃ pariṣiñcati satyaṃ tvartena pariṣiñcāmi | iti prātar |
3.5.73.d: ऋतं त्वा सत्येन परिषिञ्चामि । इति सायं परिषिञ्चति सत्यं त्वर्तेन परिषिञ्चामि । इति प्रातर् ।
3.5.73.m: "With truth I sprinkle around you, cosmic order!"—thus he sprinkles around in the evening. "With cosmic order I sprinkle around you, truth!"—thus in the morning.

3.5.73.s: evam eva hutvā pariṣiñcati | atha pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya pratyaṅṅ ādrutya jaghanena gārhapatyam upaviśyodīco 'ṅgārān nirūhya vyantān kṛtvā teṣv adhiśrityābhidyotanenābhidyotayati | agnis te tejo mā pratidhākṣīt | iti
3.5.73.d: एवम् एव हुत्वा परिषिञ्चति । अथ प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य प्रत्यङ्ङ् आद्रुत्य जघनेन गार्हपत्यम् उपविश्योदीचो ऽङ्गारान् निरूह्य व्यन्तान् कृत्वा तेष्व् अधिश्रित्याभिद्योतनेनाभिद्योतयति । अग्निस् ते तेजो मा प्रतिधाक्षीत् । इति
3.5.73.m: In this very way, having offered, he sprinkles around. Then, turning clockwise, running toward the west, sitting down behind the gārhapatya fire, scraping out embers toward the north, and separating them, having placed [the milk] on them, he illuminates it with the illuminator: "May Agni not scorch your brightness!"
With the spoon he adds water: "You are immortality."

3.5.73.s: punar evābhidyotya triḥ paryagni karoti | antaritam̐ rakṣo 'ntaritā arātayas | iti
3.5.73.d: पुनर् एवाभिद्योत्य त्रिः पर्यग्नि करोति । अन्तरितँ रक्षो ऽन्तरिता अरातयस् । इति
3.5.73.m: Illuminating it once more, he carries fire around it three times: "Warded off is the rakṣas, warded off are the enemies."

3.5.73.s: vartma kurvann udag udvāsya pratyūhyāṅgārān ādatte dakṣiṇena sruvam̐ samidhaṃ ca savyenāgnihotrahavaṇīm | devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṇṣo hastābhyām ādade | iti
3.5.73.d: वर्त्म कुर्वन्न् उदग् उद्वास्य प्रत्यूह्याङ्गारान् आदत्ते दक्षिणेन स्रुवँ समिधं च सव्येनाग्निहोत्रहवणीम् । देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूण्षो हस्ताभ्याम् आददे । इति
3.5.73.m: Making a track, taking it off toward the north, and pushing back the embers, he takes the spoon and the kindling stick with the right hand, and the agnihotra-offering ladle with the left: "At the impulse of god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take you."

3.5.73.s: gārhapatye pratitapati pratyuṣṭam̐ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayas | iti tris |
3.5.73.d: गार्हपत्ये प्रतितपति प्रत्युष्टँ रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातयस् । इति त्रिस् ।
3.5.73.m: He heats them over the gārhapatya fire: "Burnt away is the rakṣas, burnt away are the enemies," three times.

3.5.73.s: atha kūrce srucaṃ nidhāya yajamānam āmantrayate | om unneṣyāmi | iti |
3.5.73.d: अथ कूर्चे स्रुचं निधाय यजमानम् आमन्त्रयते । ओम् उन्नेष्यामि । इति ।
3.5.73.m: Then, having placed the ladle on the grass bundle, he addresses the sacrificer: "Om! I shall draw [the milk]."

3.5.73.s: atha caturaḥ sruvān unnayati pūrṇān vānūco vā bhūr iḍā bhuva iḍā suvar iḍā bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar iḍā | iti
3.5.73.d: अथ चतुरः स्रुवान् उन्नयति पूर्णान् वानूचो वा भूर् इडा भुव इडा सुवर् इडा भूर् भुवः सुवर् इडा । इति
3.5.73.m: Then he draws four spoonfuls, either full or successive: "Bhūr, the iḍā! Bhuvaḥ, the iḍā! Suvar, the iḍā! Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar, the iḍā!"

3.5.73.s: sthālyām̐ sruvaṃ pratyavadhāyāthaine saṃmṛśati sajūr devaiḥ sāyaṃyāvabhiḥ sāyaṃyāvāno mā devāḥ svasti saṃpārayantu paśubhis iti sāyam |
3.5.73.d: स्थाल्याँ स्रुवं प्रत्यवधायाथैने संमृशति सजूर् देवैः सायंयावभिः सायंयावानो मा देवाः स्वस्ति संपारयन्तु पशुभिस् इति सायम् ।
3.5.73.m: Having put the spoon back in the pot, he then touches them: "In union with the gods who go in the evening, may the gods who go in the evening carry me through safely with cattle!"—thus in the evening.

3.5.74.s: sajūr devaiḥ prātaryāvabhiḥ prātaryāvāṇo mā devāḥ svasti saṃpārayantu paśubhis | iti prātar
3.5.74.d: सजूर् देवैः प्रातर्यावभिः प्रातर्यावाणो मा देवाः स्वस्ति संपारयन्तु पशुभिस् । इति प्रातर्
3.5.74.m: "In union with the gods who go in the morning, may the gods who go in the morning carry me through safely with cattle!"—thus in the morning.

3.5.74.s: atraitām̐ samidham̐ srugdaṇḍa upasaṃgṛhya jaghanena gārhapatyam upasādayati kūrce nama īśānāya prajāḥ paśavo me vardhantām ahaṃ yajamāno mā riṣam iti
3.5.74.d: अत्रैताँ समिधँ स्रुग्दण्ड उपसंगृह्य जघनेन गार्हपत्यम् उपसादयति कूर्चे नम ईशानाय प्रजाः पशवो मे वर्धन्ताम् अहं यजमानो मा रिषम् इति
3.5.74.m: At this point, holding this kindling stick onto the handle of the ladle, he sets it down behind the gārhapatya fire on the grass bundle: "Homage to the Ruler! May my offspring and cattle increase; may I, the sacrificer, not come to harm!"

3.5.74.s: daśahotroddrutya prāṅ harati bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar urv antarikṣam anvihi | ayaṃ panthā vitato devayānas | yenāyann ṛṣayaḥ svargakāmās tena gacchāmi paramaṃ vyoma yathā na hīye sukṛtām̐ sakāśāt | iti
3.5.74.d: दशहोत्रोद्द्रुत्य प्राङ् हरति भूर् भुवः सुवर् उर्व् अन्तरिक्षम् अन्विहि । अयं पन्था विततो देवयानस् । येनायन्न् ऋषयः स्वर्गकामास् तेन गच्छामि परमं व्योम यथा न हीये सुकृताँ सकाशात् । इति
3.5.74.m: Having run up with the daśahotṛ formula, he carries it eastward: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar! Traverse the wide midspace! This path is stretched out, leading to the gods, / along which the seers went, desiring heaven; by that [path] I go to the highest firmament, so that I shall not fall away from the presence of the righteous!"

3.5.74.s: jaghanenāhavanīyam upasādayati kūrce nama īśānāya prajā me vardhatām ahaṃ yajamāno mā riṣam iti |
3.5.74.d: जघनेनाहवनीयम् उपसादयति कूर्चे नम ईशानाय प्रजा मे वर्धताम् अहं यजमानो मा रिषम् इति ।
3.5.74.m: He sets it down behind the āhavanīya fire on the grass bundle: "Homage to the Ruler! May my offspring increase; may I, the sacrificer, not come to harm!"
At this point he puts this kindling stick on the middle of the āhavanīya fire.

3.6.74.s: rajatāṃ tvāgnijyotiṣaṃ vāyumatīm̐ svargyām̐ svargāya lokāya rātrim akṣitim iṣṭakām upadadhe 'mṛtaṃ prāṇe dadhāmi prajāpatis tvā sādayatu | iti
3.6.74.d: रजतां त्वाग्निज्योतिषं वायुमतीँ स्वर्ग्याँ स्वर्गाय लोकाय रात्रिम् अक्षितिम् इष्टकाम् उपदधे ऽमृतं प्राणे दधामि प्रजापतिस् त्वा सादयतु । इति
3.6.74.m: "You, silver, having Agni's light, possessing wind, heavenly, for the heavenly world, Night, an imperishable brick I place; I place immortality in the out-breath; may Prajāpati seat you!"

3.6.74.s: tayādevataṃ karoti tayā devatayāṅgirasvad dhruvā sīda | iti |
3.6.74.d: तयादेवतं करोति तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद । इति ।
3.6.74.m: With the tayādevata formula he settles it: "With that deity, like Angiras, sit firm!"

3.6.74.s: atha sūdadohasaṃ karoti tā asya sūdadohasaḥ somam̐ śrīṇanti pṛśnayaḥ | janman devānāṃ viśas triṣvā rocane divas | iti sāyam
3.6.74.d: अथ सूददोहसं करोति ता अस्य सूददोहसः सोमँ श्रीणन्ति पृश्नयः । जन्मन् देवानां विशस् त्रिष्वा रोचने दिवस् । इति सायम्
3.6.74.m: Then he recites the sūdadohas verse: "Those nourishing milk-streams of his mix the soma, the dapple cows / at the birth of the gods, the clans, in the three luminous realms of heaven"—thus in the evening.

3.6.74.s: atha prātar hariṇīṃ tvā sūryajyotiṣaṃ vāyumatīm̐ svargyām̐ svargāya lokāyāhar akṣitim iṣṭakām upadadhe 'mṛtam apāne dadhāmi prajāpatis tvā sādayat | iti
3.6.74.d: अथ प्रातर् हरिणीं त्वा सूर्यज्योतिषं वायुमतीँ स्वर्ग्याँ स्वर्गाय लोकायाहर् अक्षितिम् इष्टकाम् उपदधे ऽमृतम् अपाने दधामि प्रजापतिस् त्वा सादयत् । इति
3.6.74.m: Then in the morning: "You, golden, having Sūrya's light, possessing wind, heavenly, for the heavenly world, Day, an imperishable brick I place; I place immortality in the in-breath; may Prajāpati seat you!"
Having recited the tayādevata formula, he recites the sūdadohas verse.

3.6.74.s: tasyām ādīptāyāṃ pratimukhaṃ juhoti | agnir jyotir jyotiḥ sūryaḥ svāhā | iti sāyam |
3.6.74.d: तस्याम् आदीप्तायां प्रतिमुखं जुहोति । अग्निर् ज्योतिर् ज्योतिः सूर्यः स्वाहा । इति सायम् ।
3.6.74.m: When it has burst into flame, he offers facing it: "Agni is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!"—thus in the evening.

3.6.75.s: sūryo jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāhā | iti prātar
3.6.75.d: सूर्यो ज्योतिर् ज्योतिर् अग्निः स्वाहा । इति प्रातर्
3.6.75.m: "Sūrya is light, light is Agni, svāhā!"—thus in the morning.

3.6.75.s: iti nu sam̐sṛṣṭam athāsam̐sṛṣṭam agnir jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāhā | iti sāyam |
3.6.75.d: इति नु सँसृष्टम् अथासँसृष्टम् अग्निर् ज्योतिर् ज्योतिर् अग्निः स्वाहा । इति सायम् ।
3.6.75.m: This is the combined [formula]. Now the uncombined [formula]: "Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!"—thus in the evening.

3.6.75.s: sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ sūryaḥ svāhā | iti prātar atha sakṛd ativālya kūrce srucaṃ nidhāya dakṣiṇāvṛd gārhapatyaṃ pratīkṣate | upapreta saṃgacchadhvaṃ mā bhāgināṃ bhāgadheyaṃ pramāyi | saptarṣīṇām̐ sukṛtām yatra lokas tatremaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca dhatta | iti |
3.6.75.d: सूर्यो ज्योतिर् ज्योतिः सूर्यः स्वाहा । इति प्रातर् अथ सकृद् अतिवाल्य कूर्चे स्रुचं निधाय दक्षिणावृद् गार्हपत्यं प्रतीक्षते । उपप्रेत संगच्छध्वं मा भागिनां भागधेयं प्रमायि । सप्तर्षीणाँ सुकृताम् यत्र लोकस् तत्रेमं यज्ञं यजमानं च धत्त । इति ।
3.6.75.m: "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!"—thus in the morning. Then, having let it drip once and having placed the ladle on the grass bundle, turning toward the south, he looks toward the gārhapatya fire: "Come near, assemble! Let not the share of the sharers perish! / Where the world of the Seven Seers of good deeds is, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer!"

3.6.75.s: atihāya pūrvām āhutim uttarāṃ bhūyaḥ samidhyeva juhoti prajāpataye svāhā | iti manasā |
3.6.75.d: अतिहाय पूर्वाम् आहुतिम् उत्तरां भूयः समिध्येव जुहोति प्रजापतये स्वाहा । इति मनसा ।
3.6.75.m: Going beyond the first oblation, he offers the second one on the flame, as it were: "To Prajāpati, svāhā!" mentally.

3.6.75.s: atha trir ativālya kūrce srucaṃ nidhāyāvācīnam avamṛjya pratīcā nīcā pāṇinauṣadhīṣu lepaṃ nimāṛṣṭi | oṣadhībhyas tvauṣadhīr jinva | iti |
3.6.75.d: अथ त्रिर् अतिवाल्य कूर्चे स्रुचं निधायावाचीनम् अवमृज्य प्रतीचा नीचा पाणिनौषधीषु लेपं निमाऋष्टि । ओषधीभ्यस् त्वौषधीर् जिन्व । इति ।
3.6.75.m: Then, having let it drip three times, having placed the ladle on the grass bundle, and having wiped [the spoon] downward, he wipes off the residue on the plants with his hand [turned] westward and downward: "For the plants, enliven the plants!"

3.6.75.s: evam eva dvitīyam avamṛjyauṣadhīṣv eva nimārṣṭi dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnāvītī pitṛbhyas tvā pitṝñ jinva | iti sāyam
3.6.75.d: एवम् एव द्वितीयम् अवमृज्यौषधीष्व् एव निमार्ष्टि दक्षिणतः प्राचीनावीती पितृभ्यस् त्वा पितॄञ् जिन्व । इति सायम्
3.6.75.m: Having wiped it a second time in the very same way, he wipes it off on the plants on the south, with the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder: "For the ancestors, enliven the ancestors!"—thus in the evening.

3.6.75.s: atha prātar ūrdhvam unmṛjya prācottānena pāṇinauṣadhīṣu lepam unmārṣṭi | oṣadhībhyas tvauṣadhīr jinva | iti |
3.6.75.d: अथ प्रातर् ऊर्ध्वम् उन्मृज्य प्राचोत्तानेन पाणिनौषधीषु लेपम् उन्मार्ष्टि । ओषधीभ्यस् त्वौषधीर् जिन्व । इति ।
3.6.75.m: Then in the morning, having wiped upward, he wipes off the residue on the plants with his hand turned eastward and upward: "For the plants, enliven the plants!"

3.6.76.s: evam eva dvitīyam avamṛjyauṣadhīṣv eva nimāṛṣṭi dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnāvītī pitṛbhyas tvā pitṝñ jinva | iti |
3.6.76.d: एवम् एव द्वितीयम् अवमृज्यौषधीष्व् एव निमाऋष्टि दक्षिणतः प्राचीनावीती पितृभ्यस् त्वा पितॄञ् जिन्व । इति ।
3.6.76.m: Having wiped it a second time in the very same way, he wipes it off on the plants on the south, with the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder: "For the ancestors, enliven the ancestors!"

3.6.76.s: athāpa upaspṛśya dvir aṅgulyā prāśnāti prajā jyotis | iti |
3.6.76.d: अथाप उपस्पृश्य द्विर् अङ्गुल्या प्राश्नाति प्रजा ज्योतिस् । इति ।
3.6.76.m: Then, having touched water, he eats twice with his finger, [saying,] “Offspring, light!”
Then, having turned around towards the north, he consumes [the remainder] from the offering ladle whose handle points eastward.

3.7.76.s: idam̐ haviḥ prajananaṃ me astu daśavīram̐ sarvagaṇam̐ savastaye | ātmasani prajāsani paśusany abhayasani lokasani vṛṣṭisani || agniḥ prajāṃ bahulāṃ me karotu | annaṃ payo reto asmāsu dhatta | rāyaspoṣam iṣam ūrjam asmāsu dīdharat svāhā | iti sāyam |
3.7.76.d: इदँ हविः प्रजननं मे अस्तु दशवीरँ सर्वगणँ सवस्तये । आत्मसनि प्रजासनि पशुसन्य् अभयसनि लोकसनि वृष्टिसनि ॥ अग्निः प्रजां बहुलां मे करोतु । अन्नं पयो रेतो अस्मासु धत्त । रायस्पोषम् इषम् ऊर्जम् अस्मासु दीधरत् स्वाहा । इति सायम् ।
3.7.76.m: “May this oblation be productive of offspring for me, / with ten heroes, with all his company, for wellbeing; / winning the self, winning offspring, / winning cattle, winning safety, winning the world, winning rain! // May Agni make my offspring abundant; / place food, milk, and seed in us; / may he sustain increase of wealth, nourishment, and strength in us, svāhā!”—[thus] in the evening.

3.7.76.s: sūryaḥ prajāṃ bahulāṃ me karotu | iti prātar
3.7.76.d: सूर्यः प्रजां बहुलां मे करोतु । इति प्रातर्
3.7.76.m: “May Sūrya make my offspring abundant”—[thus] in the morning.
